heading_path: PART 4 Procedures > DIVISION 3 Conduct of Examination > Documents Required
own_text: Subsection (1) does not apply to

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 4 Procedures > DIVISION 3 Conduct of Examination > Documents Required
own_text: citizens of the United States;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 4 Procedures > DIVISION 3 Conduct of Examination > Documents Required
own_text: persons seeking to enter Canada from the United States or St. Pierre and Miquelon who have been lawfully admitted to the United States for permanent residence;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 4 Procedures > DIVISION 3 Conduct of Examination > Documents Required
own_text: residents of Greenland seeking to enter Canada from Greenland;

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 4 Procedures > DIVISION 3 Conduct of Examination > Documents Required
own_text: persons seeking to enter Canada from St. Pierre and Miquelon who are citizens of France and residents of St. Pierre and Miquelon;

label: (e)
heading_path: PART 4 Procedures > DIVISION 3 Conduct of Examination > Documents Required
own_text: members of the armed forces of a country that is a designated state for the purposes of the Visiting Forces Act who are seeking entry in order to carry out official duties, other than persons who have been designated as a civilian component of those armed forces;

label: (f)
heading_path: PART 4 Procedures > DIVISION 3 Conduct of Examination > Documents Required
own_text: persons who are seeking to enter Canada as, or in order to become, members of a crew of a means of air transportation and who hold an airline flight crew licence or crew member certificate issued in accordance with International Civil Aviation Organization specifications; or

label: (g)
heading_path: PART 4 Procedures > DIVISION 3 Conduct of Examination > Documents Required
own_text: persons seeking to enter Canada as members of a crew who hold a seafarer’s identity document issued under International Labour Organization conventions and are members of the crew of the vessel that carries them to Canada.

heading_path: PART 4 Procedures > DIVISION 3 Conduct of Examination > Documents Required
own_text: [Repealed, SOR/2010-54, s. 3]

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: For the purposes of subsection 31(1) of the Act, the document indicating the status of a permanent resident is a permanent resident card that is

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: provided by the Department to a person who has become a permanent resident under the Act; or

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: issued by the Department, on application, to a permanent resident who has become a permanent resident under the Act or a permanent resident who obtained that status under the Immigration Act , chapter I-2 of the Revised Statutes of Canada, 1985, as it read immediately before the coming into force of section 31 of the Act.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: A permanent resident card remains the property of Her Majesty in right of Canada at all times and must be returned to the Department on the Department’s request.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: Subject to subsection (2), a permanent resident card is valid for five years from the date of issue.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: A permanent resident card is valid for one year from the date of issue if, at the time of issue, the permanent resident

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: is subject to the process set out in paragraph 46(1)(b) of the Act;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: is the subject of a report prepared under subsection 44(1) of the Act;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: is subject to a removal order made by the Minister under subsection 44(2) of the Act and the period for filing an appeal from the decision has not expired or, if an appeal is filed, there has been no final determination of the appeal; or

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: is the subject of a report referred to the Immigration Division under subsection 44(2) of the Act and the period for filing an appeal from the decision of the Immigration Division has not expired or, if an appeal is filed, there has been no final determination of the appeal.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: A permanent resident card shall only be provided or issued in Canada.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: [Repealed, SOR/2008-188, s. 1]

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: An application for a permanent resident card must be made in Canada and include

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: an application form that contains the following information, namely,

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: the applicant’s name and date and place of birth,

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: the applicant’s gender, height and eye colour,

label: (iii)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: the date on which and the place where the applicant became a permanent resident,

label: (iv)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: the applicant’s mailing address,

label: (v)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: the addresses of all of the applicant’s places of residence during the previous five years,

label: (vi)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: the names and addresses of the applicant’s employers and educational institutions attended, during the previous five years,

label: (vii)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: the periods during the previous five years that the applicant was absent from Canada,

label: (viii)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: [Repealed, SOR/2008-188, s. 1]

label: (ix)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: whether a report under subsection 44(1) of the Act has been made in respect of the applicant or whether a decision was made outside of Canada that they have failed to comply with the residency obligation under section 28 of the Act, and

label: (x)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: whether the applicant has lost their permanent resident status or has been issued a removal order;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: [Repealed, SOR/2008-188, s. 1]

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: a copy of

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: any document described in paragraphs 50(1)(a) to (h) — or, if the applicant does not hold one of those documents, any document described in paragraphs 178(1)(a) and (b) — that is currently held by the applicant or was held by the applicant at the time they became a permanent resident,

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: a certificate of identity issued in Canada to the applicant by the Minister, or

label: (iii)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: refugee travel papers issued in Canada to the applicant by the Minister;

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: a copy of

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: the form IMM1000, entitled “Record of Landing”, held by the applicant,

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: a provincial driver’s license held by the applicant,

label: (iii)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: a photo-identity card held by the applicant and issued by a province,

label: (iv)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: a student card held by the applicant and issued by a provincially accredited college or university, or

label: (v)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: the most recent notice of assessment within the meaning of the Income Tax Act received in relation to the applicant’s income tax return; and

label: (e)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: two identical photographs that

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: were taken not more than 12 months before the application was made,

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: [Repealed, SOR/2008-188, s. 1]

label: (iii)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: are in black and white or colour on paper,

label: (iv)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: show a full front view of the applicant’s head and shoulders and have a white background,

label: (v)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: have a view of the applicant’s head that is at least 25 mm (one inch) and at most 35 mm (1.375 inches) in length,

label: (vi)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: show the applicant’s face unobscured by sunglasses or any other object, and

label: (vii)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: have a dimension of 35 mm (1.375 inches) by 45 mm (1.75 inches).

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: [Repealed, SOR/2008-188, s. 1]

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: Subject to subsection (3), every person who applies for a permanent resident card must make and sign the application on their own behalf.

marginal_note: Minor applicants 14 years of age or more
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: The application of a child who is 14 years of age or more but less than 18 years of age must be signed by the applicant and one of their parents unless

label: (a)
marginal_note: Minor applicants 14 years of age or more
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: a Canadian court has made another person responsible for the child, in which case that person must co-sign the application; or

label: (b)
marginal_note: Minor applicants 14 years of age or more
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: the parents are deceased, in which case the person legally responsible for the child must co-sign the application.

marginal_note: Minor applicants less than 14 years of age
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: The application of a child who is less than 14 years of age must be signed by one of their parents unless

label: (a)
marginal_note: Minor applicants less than 14 years of age
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: a Canadian court has made another person responsible for the child, in which case that person must sign the application; or

label: (b)
marginal_note: Minor applicants less than 14 years of age
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: the parents are deceased, in which case the person legally responsible for the child must sign the application.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: In order to allow the Department to provide a permanent resident card, a permanent resident referred to in paragraph 53(1)(a) must provide to the Department, within 180 days after the day on which they become a permanent resident, their address in Canada and, on the request of an officer,

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: a photograph of the permanent resident that satisfies the requirements of subparagraphs 56(2)(e)(i) and (iii) to (vii); and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: the signature of the permanent resident or, if the permanent resident is a child less than 14 years of age, the signature of one of their parents unless

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: a Canadian court has made another person responsible for the child, in which case the signature of that person must be provided, or

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: the parents are deceased, in which case the signature of the person legally responsible for the child must be provided.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: If the permanent resident does not comply with subsection (1), they must make an application for a permanent resident card in accordance with section 56.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: A permanent resident who applies for a permanent resident card under section 56 must, in order to be provided with the card, attend at the time and place specified in a notice mailed by the Department. If the permanent resident fails to attend within 180 days after the Department first mails a notice, the card shall be destroyed and the applicant must make a new application in order to be issued a permanent resident card.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: When attending in accordance with subsection (3), a permanent resident must produce the original documents copies of which were included in their application as required by paragraphs 56(2)(c) and (d).

marginal_note: Issuance of new permanent resident card
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards

marginal_note: Issuance of new permanent resident card
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: An officer shall, on application, issue a new permanent resident card if

label: (a)
marginal_note: Issuance of new permanent resident card
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: the applicant has not lost permanent resident status under subsection 46(1) of the Act;

label: (b)
marginal_note: Issuance of new permanent resident card
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: the applicant has not been convicted under section 123 or 126 of the Act for an offence related to the misuse of a permanent resident card, unless a pardon has been granted and has not ceased to have effect or been revoked under the Criminal Records Act ;

label: (c)
marginal_note: Issuance of new permanent resident card
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: the applicant complies with the requirements of sections 56 and 57 and subsection 58(4);

label: (c.1)
marginal_note: Issuance of new permanent resident card
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: in the case of an applicant referred to in paragraph 12.1(m) who is 14 years of age or older, the applicant has provided their biometric information in support of their application; and

label: (d)
marginal_note: Issuance of new permanent resident card
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: the applicant returns their last permanent resident card, unless the card has been lost, stolen or destroyed, in which case the applicant must produce all relevant evidence in accordance with subsection 16(1) of the Act.

marginal_note: Issuance of new permanent resident card — effect
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: A previously issued permanent resident card is revoked on the issuance of a new permanent resident card.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: A permanent resident card is revoked if

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: the permanent resident becomes a Canadian citizen or otherwise loses permanent resident status;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: the permanent resident card is lost, stolen or destroyed; or

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1 Permanent Resident Cards
own_text: the permanent resident is deceased.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1.1 Collection and Disclosure of Information
PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1.1 Collection and Disclosure of Information
own_text: The Minister may collect the social insurance number of a permanent resident card applicant or a travel document applicant to verify that the applicant has complied with the obligation set out in section 28 of the Act.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 1.1 Collection and Disclosure of Information
own_text: The Minister may disclose the social insurance number of the applicant to the Canada Revenue Agency for the purpose set out in subsection (1) if the Minister has entered into an arrangement with the Agency for the disclosure of that information.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 2 Residency Obligation
PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 2 Residency Obligation
own_text: Subject to subsection (2), for the purposes of subparagraphs 28(2)(a)(iii) and (iv) of the Act and of this section, a Canadian business is

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 2 Residency Obligation
own_text: a corporation that is incorporated under the laws of Canada or of a province and that has an ongoing operation in Canada;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 2 Residency Obligation
own_text: an enterprise, other than a corporation described in paragraph (a), that has an ongoing operation in Canada and

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 2 Residency Obligation
own_text: that is capable of generating revenue and is carried on in anticipation of profit, and

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 2 Residency Obligation
own_text: in which a majority of voting or ownership interests is held by Canadian citizens, permanent residents, or Canadian businesses as defined in this subsection; or

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 2 Residency Obligation
own_text: an organization or enterprise created under the laws of Canada or a province.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 2 Residency Obligation
own_text: For greater certainty, a Canadian business does not include a business that serves primarily to allow a permanent resident to comply with their residency obligation while residing outside Canada.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 2 Residency Obligation
own_text: For the purposes of subparagraphs 28(2)(a)(iii) and (iv) of the Act, the expression employed on a full-time basis by a Canadian business or in the public service of Canada or of a province means, in relation to a permanent resident, that the permanent resident is an employee of, or under contract to provide services to, a Canadian business or the public service of Canada or of a province, and is assigned on a full-time basis as a term of the employment or contract to

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 2 Residency Obligation
own_text: a position outside Canada;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 2 Residency Obligation
own_text: an affiliated enterprise outside Canada; or

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 2 Residency Obligation
own_text: a client of the Canadian business or the public service outside Canada.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 2 Residency Obligation
own_text: For the purposes of subparagraphs 28(2)(a)(ii) and (iv) of the Act and this section, a permanent resident is accompanying outside Canada a Canadian citizen or another permanent resident — who is their spouse or common-law partner or, in the case of a child, their parent — on each day that the permanent resident is ordinarily residing with the Canadian citizen or the other permanent resident.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 2 Residency Obligation
own_text: For the purposes of subparagraph 28(2)(a)(iv) of the Act, a permanent resident complies with the residency obligation as long as the permanent resident they are accompanying complies with their residency obligation.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 2 Residency Obligation
own_text: For the purposes of subparagraphs 28(2)(a)(ii) and (iv) of the Act, child means a child who is not a spouse or common-law partner and is less than 22 years of age.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 2 Residency Obligation
PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 2 Residency Obligation
own_text: Subject to subsection (2), the calculation of days under paragraph 28(2)(a) of the Act in respect of a permanent resident does not include any day after

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 2 Residency Obligation
own_text: a report is prepared under subsection 44(1) of the Act on the ground that the permanent resident has failed to comply with the residency obligation; or

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 2 Residency Obligation
own_text: a decision is made outside of Canada that the permanent resident has failed to comply with the residency obligation.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 2 Residency Obligation
own_text: If the permanent resident is subsequently determined to have complied with the residency obligation, subsection (1) does not apply.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 3 Permit Holders
own_text: A temporary resident permit is valid until any one of the following events occurs:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 3 Permit Holders
own_text: the permit is cancelled under subsection 24(1) of the Act or under section 243.1;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 3 Permit Holders
own_text: the permit holder leaves Canada without obtaining prior authorization to re-enter Canada;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 3 Permit Holders
own_text: the period of validity specified on the permit expires; or

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 3 Permit Holders
own_text: a period of three years elapses from its date of validity.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: The permit holder class is prescribed as a class of foreign nationals who may become permanent residents on the basis of the requirements of this Division.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: A foreign national is a permit holder and a member of the permit holder class if

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: they have been issued a temporary resident permit under subsection 24(1) of the Act;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: they have continuously resided in Canada as a permit holder for a period of

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: at least three years, if they

label: (A)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: are inadmissible on health grounds under subsection 38(1) of the Act,

label: (B)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: are inadmissible under paragraph 42(1)(a) of the Act on grounds of an accompanying family member who is inadmissible under subsection 38(1) of the Act, or

label: (C)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: are inadmissible under paragraph 42(1)(b) of the Act on grounds of being an accompanying family member of a foreign national who is inadmissible

label: (I)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: under subsection 38(1) of the Act, or

label: (II)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: under paragraph 42(1)(a) of the Act on grounds of an accompanying family member who is inadmissible under subsection 38(1) of the Act,

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: at least five years, if they are inadmissible on any other grounds under the Act, except sections 34 to 35.1 and subsections 36(1) and 37(1) of the Act;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: they have not become inadmissible on any ground since the permit was issued; and

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: in the case of a foreign national who intends to reside in the Province of Quebec and is not a member of the family class or a person whom the Board has determined to be a Convention refugee, the competent authority of that Province is of the opinion that the foreign national meets the selection criteria of the Province.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: A foreign national in Canada who is a permit holder and a member of the permit holder class becomes a permanent resident if, following an examination, it is established that

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: they have applied to remain in Canada as a permanent resident as a member of that class;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: they are in Canada to establish permanent residence;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: they meet the selection criteria and other requirements applicable to that class;

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: they hold

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: subject to subsection (4), a document described in any of paragraphs 50(1)(a) to (h), and

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: a medical certificate — based on the most recent medical examination to which they were required to submit under paragraph 16(2)(b) of the Act and which took place within the previous 12 months — that indicates that their health condition is not likely to be a danger to public health or public safety and is not reasonably expected to cause excessive demand; and

label: (e)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: they and their family members, whether accompanying or not, are not inadmissible on any ground other than the grounds on which an officer, at the time the permit was issued, formed the opinion that the foreign national was inadmissible.

marginal_note: Criteria in the Province of Quebec
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: For the purposes of paragraph (1)(c), the selection criterion applicable to a foreign national who intends to reside in the Province of Quebec as a permanent resident and who is not a person whom the Board has determined to be a Convention refugee is met by evidence that the competent authority of that Province is of the opinion that the foreign national meets the selection criteria of the Province.

marginal_note: Foreign nationals without a passport or other travel document
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: The following foreign nationals who are not holders of a document described in any of paragraphs 50(1)(a) to (h) may submit with their application a document described in paragraph 178(1)(a) or (b):

label: (a)
marginal_note: Foreign nationals without a passport or other travel document
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: a protected person within the meaning of subsection 95(2) of the Act;

label: (b)
marginal_note: Foreign nationals without a passport or other travel document
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: a person who was determined to be a Convention refugee seeking resettlement under the Immigration Regulations, 1978 , as enacted by Order in Council P.C. 1978-486 dated February 23, 1978 and registered as SOR/78-172, if under the Act or section 69.2 of the former Act, within the meaning of section 187 of the Act,

label: (i)
marginal_note: Foreign nationals without a passport or other travel document
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: no determination has been made to vacate that determination, or

label: (ii)
marginal_note: Foreign nationals without a passport or other travel document
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: no determination has been made that the person ceased to be a Convention refugee; and

label: (c)
marginal_note: Foreign nationals without a passport or other travel document
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: a member of the country of asylum class or the source country class under the Humanitarian Designated Classes Regulations , as enacted by Order in Council P.C. 1997-477 dated April 8, 1997 and registered as SOR/97-183.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 4 Permit Holders Class
own_text: A document submitted under subsection (3) shall be accepted in lieu of a document described in any of paragraphs 50(1)(a) to (h) if it satisfies the requirements of paragraphs 178(2)(a) or (b).

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 5 Humanitarian and Compassionate Considerations
own_text: A request made by a foreign national under subsection 25(1) of the Act must be made as an application in writing accompanied by an application to remain in Canada as a permanent resident or, in the case of a foreign national outside Canada, an application for a permanent resident visa.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 5 Humanitarian and Compassionate Considerations
own_text: If an exemption from paragraphs 70(1)(a), (c) and (d) is granted under subsection 25(1), 25.1(1) or 25.2(1) of the Act with respect to a foreign national outside Canada who has made the applications referred to in section 66, a permanent resident visa shall be issued to the foreign national if, following an examination, it is established that the foreign national meets the requirement set out in paragraph 70(1)(b) and

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 5 Humanitarian and Compassionate Considerations
own_text: in the case of a foreign national who intends to reside in the Province of Quebec and is not a member of the family class, the competent authority of that Province is of the opinion that the foreign national meets the selection criteria of the Province;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 5 Humanitarian and Compassionate Considerations
own_text: the foreign national is not otherwise inadmissible; and

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 5 Humanitarian and Compassionate Considerations
own_text: the family members of the foreign national, whether accompanying or not, are not inadmissible.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 5 Humanitarian and Compassionate Considerations
own_text: If an exemption from paragraphs 72(1)(a), (c) and (d) is granted under subsection 25(1), 25.1(1) or 25.2(1) of the Act with respect to a foreign national in Canada who has made the applications referred to in section 66, the foreign national becomes a permanent resident if, following an examination, it is established that the foreign national meets the requirements set out in paragraphs 72(1)(b) and (e) and

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 5 Humanitarian and Compassionate Considerations
own_text: in the case of a foreign national who intends to reside in the Province of Quebec and is not a member of the family class or a person whom the Board has determined to be a Convention refugee, the competent authority of that Province is of the opinion that the foreign national meets the selection criteria of the Province;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 5 Humanitarian and Compassionate Considerations
own_text: the foreign national is not otherwise inadmissible; and

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 5 Humanitarian and Compassionate Considerations
own_text: the family members of the foreign national, whether accompanying or not, are not inadmissible.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 5 Humanitarian and Compassionate Considerations
PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 5 Humanitarian and Compassionate Considerations
own_text: A foreign national who is an accompanying family member of a foreign national to whom a permanent resident visa is issued under section 67 shall be issued a permanent resident visa if, following an examination, it is established that

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 5 Humanitarian and Compassionate Considerations
own_text: the accompanying family member is not inadmissible; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 5 Humanitarian and Compassionate Considerations
own_text: in the case of an accompanying family member who intends to reside in the Province of Quebec and is not a member of the family class or a person whom the Board has determined to be a Convention refugee, the competent authority of that Province is of the opinion that the family member meets the selection criteria of the Province.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 5 Humanitarian and Compassionate Considerations
own_text: A foreign national who is an accompanying family member of a foreign national who becomes a permanent resident under section 68 shall become a permanent resident if the accompanying family member is in Canada and, following an examination, it is established that

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 5 Humanitarian and Compassionate Considerations
own_text: the accompanying family member is not inadmissible; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 5 Humanitarian and Compassionate Considerations
own_text: in the case of an accompanying family member who intends to reside in the Province of Quebec and is not a member of the family class or a person whom the Board has determined to be a Convention refugee, the competent authority of that Province is of the opinion that the family member meets the selection criteria of the Province.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 5 Humanitarian and Compassionate Considerations
own_text: Subject to subsection 25.1(1), to be considered a family member of the applicant, a person shall be a family member of an applicant both at the time the application under section 66 is made and at the time of the determination of the application.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 6 Permanent Resident Visa
PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 6 Permanent Resident Visa
own_text: An officer shall issue a permanent resident visa to a foreign national if, following an examination, it is established that

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 6 Permanent Resident Visa
own_text: the foreign national has applied in accordance with these Regulations for a permanent resident visa as a member of a class referred to in subsection (2);

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 6 Permanent Resident Visa
own_text: the foreign national is coming to Canada to establish permanent residence;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 6 Permanent Resident Visa
own_text: the foreign national is a member of that class;

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 6 Permanent Resident Visa
own_text: the foreign national meets the selection criteria and other requirements applicable to that class; and

label: (e)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 6 Permanent Resident Visa
own_text: the foreign national and their family members, whether accompanying or not, are not inadmissible.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 6 Permanent Resident Visa
own_text: The classes are

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 6 Permanent Resident Visa
own_text: the family class;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 6 Permanent Resident Visa
own_text: the economic class, consisting of the federal skilled worker class, the Quebec skilled worker class, the provincial nominee class, the Canadian experience class, the federal skilled trades class, the Atlantic immigration class, the rural community immigration class, the Quebec investor class, the Quebec entrepreneur class, the start-up business class, the self-employed persons class and the Quebec self-employed persons class; and

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 6 Permanent Resident Visa
own_text: the Convention refugees abroad class and the country of asylum class.

marginal_note: Criteria in the Province of Quebec
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 6 Permanent Resident Visa
own_text: For the purposes of paragraph (1)(d), the selection criterion for a foreign national who intends to reside in the Province of Quebec as a permanent resident and is not a member of the family class is met by evidence that the competent authority of that Province is of the opinion that the foreign national complies with the provincial selection criteria.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 6 Permanent Resident Visa
own_text: A foreign national who is an accompanying family member of a foreign national who is issued a permanent resident visa shall be issued a permanent resident visa if, following an examination, it is established that

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 6 Permanent Resident Visa
own_text: the accompanying family member is not inadmissible; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 6 Permanent Resident Visa
own_text: in the case of a family member who intends to reside in the Province of Quebec and is not a member of the family class, the competent authority of that Province is of the opinion that the family member complies with the provincial selection criteria.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 6 Permanent Resident Visa
own_text: If a permanent resident visa is not issued to a child as an accompanying family member of a foreign national or the foreign national’s spouse or common-law partner, a permanent resident visa shall not be issued to a child of that child as an accompanying family member of the foreign national.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 6 Permanent Resident Visa
own_text: An officer shall issue a permanent resident visa to a foreign national outside Canada who intends to reside in the Province of Quebec as a permanent resident and does not satisfy the requirements of paragraphs 70(1)(a), (c) and (d) if, following an examination, it is established that

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 6 Permanent Resident Visa
own_text: the foreign national has applied for a permanent resident visa in accordance with these Regulations, other than paragraph 10(2)(c);

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 6 Permanent Resident Visa
own_text: the foreign national may not be issued a permanent resident visa under subsection 176(2) and is not a member of any class of persons prescribed by these Regulations who may become permanent residents or be issued permanent resident visas;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 6 Permanent Resident Visa
own_text: the foreign national is named in a Certificat de sélection du Québec issued by that Province indicating that the foreign national, under the regulations made under An Act respecting immigration to Québec , R.S.Q., c. I-0.2, as amended from time to time, is a foreign national in a particularly distressful situation; and

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 6 Permanent Resident Visa
own_text: the foreign national and their family members, whether accompanying or not, are not inadmissible.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 7 Becoming a Permanent Resident
PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 7 Becoming a Permanent Resident
own_text: A foreign national who is a member of a class referred to in subsection 70(2) and is outside Canada must, to become a permanent resident, present their permanent resident visa to an officer at a port of entry.

marginal_note: Foreign nationals in Canada as temporary residents
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 7 Becoming a Permanent Resident
own_text: A foreign national who is a member of a class referred to in paragraph 70(2)(a) or (b) and who is a temporary resident in Canada must, to become a permanent resident, present their permanent resident visa to an officer at a port of entry or at an office of the Department in Canada.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 7 Becoming a Permanent Resident
PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 7 Becoming a Permanent Resident
own_text: A foreign national in Canada becomes a permanent resident if, following an examination, it is established that

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 7 Becoming a Permanent Resident
own_text: they have applied to remain in Canada as a permanent resident as a member of a class referred to in subsection (2);

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 7 Becoming a Permanent Resident
own_text: they are in Canada to establish permanent residence;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 7 Becoming a Permanent Resident
own_text: they are a member of that class;

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 7 Becoming a Permanent Resident
own_text: they meet the selection criteria and other requirements applicable to that class;

label: (e)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 7 Becoming a Permanent Resident
own_text: except in the case of a foreign national who has submitted a document accepted under subsection 178(2) or of a member of the protected temporary residents class,

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 7 Becoming a Permanent Resident
own_text: they and their family members, whether accompanying or not, are not inadmissible,

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 7 Becoming a Permanent Resident
own_text: they hold a document described in any of paragraphs 50(1)(a) to (h), and

label: (iii)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 7 Becoming a Permanent Resident
own_text: they hold a medical certificate — based on the most recent medical examination to which they were required to submit under paragraph 16(2)(b) of the Act and which took place within the previous 12 months — that indicates that their health condition is not likely to be a danger to public health or public safety and, unless subsection 38(2) of the Act applies, is not reasonably expected to cause excessive demand; and

label: (f)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 7 Becoming a Permanent Resident
own_text: in the case of a member of the protected temporary residents class, they are not inadmissible.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 7 Becoming a Permanent Resident
own_text: The classes are

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 7 Becoming a Permanent Resident
own_text: [Repealed, SOR/2017-78, s. 4]

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 7 Becoming a Permanent Resident
own_text: the spouse or common-law partner in Canada class; and

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 7 Becoming a Permanent Resident
own_text: the protected temporary residents class.

marginal_note: Criteria in the Province of Quebec
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 7 Becoming a Permanent Resident
own_text: For the purposes of paragraph (1)(d), the selection criterion applicable to a foreign national who intends to reside in the Province of Quebec as a permanent resident, and who is not a member of the family class or a person whom the Board has determined to be a Convention refugee, is met by evidence that the competent authority of that Province is of the opinion that the foreign national meets the selection criteria of the Province.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 7 Becoming a Permanent Resident
own_text: A foreign national who is an accompanying family member of a foreign national who becomes a permanent resident under this section shall be issued a permanent resident visa or become a permanent resident, as the case may be, if following an examination it is established that

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 7 Becoming a Permanent Resident
own_text: the accompanying family member is not inadmissible;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 7 Becoming a Permanent Resident
own_text: in the case of a family member who intends to reside in the Province of Quebec and is not a member of the family class or a person whom the Board has determined to be a Convention refugee, the competent authority of that Province is of the opinion that the family member meets the selection criteria of the Province.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 9 Application to Renounce Permanent Resident Status
own_text: Despite subsection 10(3), a separate application must be made for each family member that would like to renounce their permanent resident status.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 9 Application to Renounce Permanent Resident Status
own_text: An officer may approve a person’s application to renounce their permanent resident status if

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 9 Application to Renounce Permanent Resident Status
own_text: the person has provided evidence of their citizenship, nationality or permanent legal resident status in another country; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 9 Application to Renounce Permanent Resident Status
own_text: in the case of an application in respect of a person who is less than 18 years of age, the application is signed by every person who has custody of that person or who is empowered to act on their behalf by virtue of a court order or written agreement or by operation of law, unless otherwise ordered by a court.

heading_path: PART 5 Permanent Residents > DIVISION 9 Application to Renounce Permanent Resident Status
own_text: If a permanent resident makes an application to renounce their permanent resident status, any sponsorship application made by them is suspended until a decision is made on the application to renounce permanent residence.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 0.1 General
own_text: Subject to subsections 25.1(3) to (5) and for the purposes of this Part, to be considered a family member of an applicant, a person must be a family member of the applicant both at the time the application under Division 6 of Part 5 is made and at the time of the determination of the application.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Interpretation
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Interpretation
own_text: The following definitions apply in this Division. Atlantic province means Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island or Newfoundland and Labrador. ( province de l’Atlantique ) Canadian educational credential means any secondary school diploma or any post-secondary diploma, certificate or credential that is issued on the completion of a Canadian program of study or training at an educational or training institution that is recognized by the provincial authorities responsible for registering, accrediting, supervising and regulating such institutions. ( diplôme canadien ) educational credential [Repealed, SOR/2012-274, s. 3] equivalency assessment means a determination, issued by an organization or institution designated under subsection 75(4), that a foreign diploma, certificate or credential is equivalent to a Canadian educational credential and an assessment, by the organization or institution, of the authenticity of the foreign diploma, certificate or credential. ( attestation d’équivalence ) former Regulations has the same meaning as in subsection 316(1). ( ancien règlement ) full-time work means at least 30 hours of work over a period of one week. ( travail à temps plein ) language skill area means speaking, oral comprehension, reading or writing. ( habileté langagière ) restricted occupation means an occupation designated as a restricted occupation by the Minister, taking into account labour market activity on both an area and a national basis, following consultation with the Department of Employment and Social Development, provincial governments and any other relevant organizations or institutions. ( profession d’accès limité )

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Interpretation
own_text: Despite the definition work in section 2, for the purposes of this Division, work means an activity for which wages are paid or commission is earned.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > General
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > General
own_text: For the purposes of paragraphs 75(2)(d), 79(3)(a), 87.1(2)(d) and (e), 87.2(3)(a), 87.3(2)(f) and 87.4(2)(f), the Minister shall fix, by class prescribed by these Regulations or by occupation, and make available to the public, minimum language proficiency thresholds on the basis of

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > General
own_text: the number of applications in all classes under this Part that are being processed;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > General
own_text: the number of immigrants who are projected to become permanent residents according to the report to Parliament referred to in section 94 of the Act; and

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > General
own_text: the potential, taking into account the applicants’ linguistic profiles and economic and other relevant factors, for the establishment in Canada of applicants under the federal skilled worker class, the Canadian experience class, the federal skilled trades class, the Atlantic immigration class and the rural community immigration class.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > General
own_text: The minimum language proficiency thresholds fixed by the Minister shall be established in reference to the benchmarks described in the Canadian Language Benchmarks and the Niveaux de compétence linguistique canadiens .

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > General
own_text: The Minister may designate, for any period he or she specifies, any organization or institution to be responsible for evaluating language proficiency and approve the language test to be used to evaluate that proficiency if the organization or institution

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > General
own_text: has expertise in evaluating language proficiency; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > General
own_text: has provided the Minister with an equivalency between its language test results and the benchmarks set out in the Canadian Language Benchmarks or the Niveaux de compétence linguistique canadiens , as the case may be.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > General
own_text: The Minister shall make available to the public the names of the designated organizations or institutions and the approved language tests.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > General
own_text: For the purpose of subsection (6), service agreement means an agreement concluded between the Government of Canada and an organization or institution for the purpose of having the organization or institution supply the service of evaluating the language proficiency of foreign nationals.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > General
own_text: The Minister may revoke a designation of an organization or institution or the approval of a language test if

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > General
own_text: the organization or institution no longer meets the criteria set out in subsection (3);

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > General
own_text: the organization or institution submitted false, misleading or inaccurate information or has contravened any provision of a federal or provincial law or regulation that is relevant to the service provided by the organization or institution; or

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > General
own_text: either the Government of Canada or the organization or institution has terminated the service agreement.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > General
own_text: The results of an evaluation of language proficiency by a designated organization or institution using an approved language test are conclusive evidence of an applicant’s language proficiency in respect of the federal skilled worker class, the Canadian experience class, the federal skilled trades class, the Atlantic immigration class or the rural community immigration class.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: For the purposes of subsection 12(2) of the Act, the federal skilled worker class is hereby prescribed as a class of persons who are skilled workers and who may become permanent residents on the basis of their ability to become economically established in Canada and who intend to reside in a province other than the Province of Quebec.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: A foreign national is a skilled worker if

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: within the 10 years before the date on which their application for a permanent resident visa is made, they have accumulated, over a continuous period, at least one year of full-time work experience, or the equivalent in part-time work, in the occupation that they identified in their application as their primary occupation, other than a restricted occupation, that is listed in TEER Category 0, 1, 2 or 3 of the National Occupational Classification ;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: during that period of employment they performed the actions described in the lead statement for the occupation as set out in the occupational descriptions of the National Occupational Classification ;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: during that period of employment they performed a substantial number of the main duties of the occupation as set out in the occupational descriptions of the National Occupational Classification , including all of the essential duties;

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: they have submitted the results of a language test that is approved under subsection 74(3), which results must be provided by an organization or institution that is designated under that subsection, must be less than two years old on the date on which their application for a permanent resident visa is made and must indicate that they have met or exceeded the applicable language proficiency threshold in either English or French that is fixed by the Minister under subsection 74(1) for each of the four language skill areas; and

label: (e)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: they have submitted one of the following:

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: their Canadian educational credential, or

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: their foreign diploma, certificate or credential and the equivalency assessment, which assessment must be less than five years old on the date on which their application is made.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: If a professional body has been designated under subsection (4) in respect of the occupation identified by the foreign national in their application as their primary occupation, the foreign diploma, certificate or credential submitted by the foreign national must be relevant to that occupation and the equivalency assessment — which must be less than five years old on the date on which their application is made and must be issued by the designated professional body — must establish that the foreign diploma, certificate or credential is equivalent to the Canadian educational credential required to practise that occupation in at least one of the provinces in which the equivalency assessments issued by this professional body are recognized.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: If the foreign national fails to meet the requirements of subsection (2), the application for a permanent resident visa shall be refused and no further assessment is required.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: For the purposes of paragraph (2)(e) and subsection (2.1), the Minister may designate, for a period specified by the Minister, any organization or institution to be responsible for issuing equivalency assessments

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: if the organization or institution has the recognized expertise to assess the authenticity of foreign diplomas, certificates and credentials and their equivalency to Canadian educational credentials; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: if, in the case of a professional body, its equivalency assessments are recognized by at least two provincial professional bodies that regulate an occupation listed in TEER Category 1, 2 or 3 of the National Occupational Classification for which licensing by a provincial regulatory body is required.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: The Minister shall make available to the public a list of the designated organizations or institutions.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: For the purpose of subsection (7), service agreement means an agreement concluded between the Government of Canada and an organization or institution for the purpose of having the organization or institution supply the service of assessing the authenticity of foreign diplomas, certificates and credentials and their equivalency to Canadian educational credentials.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: The Minister may revoke a designation if

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: the organization or institution no longer meets the criteria set out in subsection (4);

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: the organization or institution submitted false, misleading or inaccurate information or has contravened any provision of federal or provincial legislation relevant to the service provided by the organization or institution; or

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: either the Government of Canada or the organization or institution has terminated the service agreement.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: For the purposes of paragraph (2)(e), subsection (2.1) and section 78, an equivalency assessment is conclusive evidence that the foreign diplomas, certificates or credentials are equivalent to Canadian educational credentials.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: For the purpose of determining whether a skilled worker, as a member of the federal skilled worker class, will be able to become economically established in Canada, they must be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: the skilled worker must be awarded not less than the minimum number of required points referred to in subsection (2) on the basis of the following factors, namely,

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: education, in accordance with section 78,

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: proficiency in the official languages of Canada, in accordance with section 79,

label: (iii)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: experience, in accordance with section 80,

label: (iv)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: age, in accordance with section 81,

label: (v)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: arranged employment, in accordance with section 82, and

label: (vi)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: adaptability, in accordance with section 83; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: the skilled worker must

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: have in the form of transferable and available funds, unencumbered by debts or other obligations, an amount equal to one half of the minimum necessary income applicable in respect of the group of persons consisting of the skilled worker and their family members, or

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: be awarded points under paragraph 82(2)(a), (b) or (d) for arranged employment, as defined in subsection 82(1), in Canada.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: The Minister shall fix and make available to the public the minimum number of points required of a skilled worker, on the basis of

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: the number of applications by skilled workers as members of the federal skilled worker class currently being processed;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: the number of skilled workers projected to become permanent residents according to the report to Parliament referred to in section 94 of the Act; and

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: the potential, taking into account economic and other relevant factors, for the establishment of skilled workers in Canada.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: Whether or not the skilled worker has been awarded the minimum number of required points referred to in subsection (2), an officer may substitute for the criteria set out in paragraph (1)(a) their evaluation of the likelihood of the ability of the skilled worker to become economically established in Canada if the number of points awarded is not a sufficient indicator of whether the skilled worker may become economically established in Canada.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: An evaluation made under subsection (3) requires the concurrence of a second officer.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Worker Class
own_text: For the purposes of Part 5, the requirements and criteria set out in sections 75 and 76 must be met on the date on which an application for a permanent resident visa is made and on the date on which it is issued.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: Points shall be awarded, to a maximum of 25, for a skilled worker’s Canadian educational credential or equivalency assessment submitted in support of an application, as follows:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: 5 points for a secondary school credential;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: 15 points for a one-year post-secondary program credential;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: 19 points for a two-year post-secondary program credential;

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: 21 points for a post-secondary program credential of three years or longer;

label: (e)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: 22 points for two or more post-secondary program credentials, one of which must be a credential issued on completion of a post-secondary program of three years or longer;

label: (f)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: 23 points for a university-level credential at the master’s level or an entry-to-practice professional degree for an occupation listed in TEER Category 1 of the National Occupational Classification for which licensing by a provincial regulatory body is required; and

label: (g)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: 25 points for a university-level credential at the doctoral level.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: For the purposes of subsection (1), points

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: except as set out in paragraph (1)(e), shall not be awarded cumulatively on the basis of more than one educational credential; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: shall be awarded on the basis of the Canadian educational credentials or equivalency assessments submitted in support of an application for a permanent resident visa that result in the highest number of points.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: A skilled worker must identify in their application for a permanent resident visa which language — English or French — is to be considered their first official language in Canada. They must have their proficiency in that language evaluated by an organization or institution that is designated under subsection 74(3) using a language test that is approved under that subsection.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: If the skilled worker wishes to claim points for proficiency in their second official language, they must submit, in support of the application for a permanent resident visa, the results of a language test that is approved under subsection 74(3) , which results must be provided by an organization or institution that is designated under that subsection and must be less than two years old on the date on which their application is made.

marginal_note: Proficiency in English and French (28 points)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: Points for proficiency in the official languages of Canada shall be awarded up to a maximum of 24 points for the skilled worker’s first official language and a maximum of 4 points for the applicant’s second official language based on benchmarks set out in Canadian Language Benchmarks and the Niveaux de compétence linguistique canadiens , as follows:

label: (a)
marginal_note: Proficiency in English and French (28 points)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: for the four language skill areas in the skilled worker’s first official language,

label: (i)
marginal_note: Proficiency in English and French (28 points)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: 4 points per language skill area if the skilled worker’s proficiency meets the threshold fixed by the Minister under subsection 74(1) for that language skill area,

label: (ii)
marginal_note: Proficiency in English and French (28 points)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: 5 points per language skill area if the skilled worker’s proficiency exceeds the threshold fixed by the Minister under subsection 74(1) for that language skill area by one benchmark level, and

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: 6 points per language skill area if the skilled worker’s proficiency exceeds the threshold fixed by the Minister under subsection 74(1) for that language skill area by at least two benchmark levels; and

label: (b)
marginal_note: Proficiency in English and French (28 points)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: for the four language skill areas in the skilled worker’s second official language, 4 points if the skilled worker’s proficiency in that language meets or exceeds benchmark level 5 in each of the four language skill areas.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: Points shall be awarded, up to a maximum of 15 points, to a skilled worker for full-time work experience, or the equivalent in part-time work, within the 10 years before the date on which their application is made, as follows:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: 9 points for one year of work experience;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: 11 points for two to three years of work experience;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: 13 points for four to five years of work experience; and

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: 15 points for six or more years of work experience.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: For the purposes of subsection (1), points are awarded for work experience in occupations, other than a restricted occupation, that are listed in TEER Category 0, 1, 2 or 3 of the National Occupational Classification .

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: For the purposes of subsection (1), a skilled worker is considered to have experience in an occupation, regardless of whether they meet the employment requirements of the occupation as set out in the occupational descriptions of the National Occupational Classification , if they performed

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: the actions described in the lead statement for the occupation as set out in the occupational descriptions of the National Occupational Classification ; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: at least a substantial number of the main duties of the occupation as set out in the occupational descriptions of the National Occupational Classification , including all the essential duties.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: A period of work experience in one occupation that exceeds 30 hours per week, or simultaneous periods of work experience in more than one full-time occupation, is to be evaluated as a single period of full-time work experience in a single occupation.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: A skilled worker must specify in their application for a permanent resident visa the five-digit code in the National Occupational Classification that corresponds to each of the occupations that is engaged in by the applicant and that constitutes the skilled worker’s work experience.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: An officer is not required to consider occupations that have not been specified in the application.

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: 11 points for a skilled worker 36 years of age;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 1 Skilled Workers > Federal Skilled Workers > Selection Grid
own_text: 10 points for a skilled worker 37 years of age;
