heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > General
own_text: For the purposes of this Division, an applicant in the self-employed persons class or an applicant in the start-up business class is not considered to have met the applicable requirements of this Division if the fulfillment of those requirements is based on one or more transactions that were entered into primarily for the purpose of acquiring a status or privilege under the Act rather than

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > General
own_text: in the case of an applicant in the self-employed class, for the purpose of self-employment; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > General
own_text: in the case of an applicant in the start-up business class, for the purpose of engaging in the business activity for which a commitment referred to in paragraph 98.01 (2)(a) was intended.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > General
own_text: A foreign national who is an accompanying family member of a person who makes an application as a member of the Quebec investor class, the Quebec entrepreneur class, the start-up business class, the self-employed persons class or the Quebec self-employed persons class shall become a permanent resident if, following an examination, it is established that

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > General
own_text: the person who made the application has become a permanent resident; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > General
own_text: the foreign national is not inadmissible.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Quebec Investor Class
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Quebec Investor Class
own_text: For the purposes of subsection 12(2) of the Act, the Quebec investor class is prescribed as a class of persons who may become permanent residents on the basis of their ability to become economically established in Canada.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Quebec Investor Class
own_text: A foreign national is a member of the Quebec investor class if they

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Quebec Investor Class
own_text: intend to reside in Quebec; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Quebec Investor Class
own_text: are named in a Certificat de sélection du Québec issued by Quebec.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Quebec Investor Class

PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Quebec Entrepreneur Class
own_text: For the purposes of subsection 12(2) of the Act, the Quebec entrepreneur class is prescribed as a class of persons who may become permanent residents on the basis of their ability to become economically established in Canada.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Quebec Entrepreneur Class
own_text: A foreign national is a member of the Quebec entrepreneur class if they

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Quebec Entrepreneur Class
own_text: intend to reside in Quebec; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Quebec Entrepreneur Class

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: For the purposes of subsection 12(2) of the Act, the start-up business class is prescribed as a class of persons who may become permanent residents on the basis of their ability to become economically established in Canada, who meet the requirements of subsection (2) and who intend to reside in a province other than Quebec.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: A foreign national is a member of the start-up business class if

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: they have obtained a commitment that is made by one or more entities designated under subsection 98.03 (1), that is less than six months old on the date on which their application for a permanent resident visa is made and that meets the requirements of section 98.04 ;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: they have submitted the results of a language test that is approved under subsection 102.3 (4), which results must be provided by an organization or institution that is designated under that subsection, be less than two years old on the date on which their application for a permanent resident visa is made and indicate that the foreign national has met at least benchmark level 5 in either official language for all four language skill areas, as set out in the Canadian Language Benchmarks or the Niveaux de compétence linguistique canadiens , as applicable;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: they have, excluding any investment made by a designated entity into their business, transferable and available funds unencumbered by debts or other obligations of an amount that is equal to one half of the amount identified, in the most recent edition of the publication concerning low income cut-offs published annually by Statistics Canada under the Statistics Act , for urban areas of residence of 500,000 persons or more, as the minimum amount of before-tax annual income that is necessary to support a group of persons equal in number to the total number of the applicant and their family members; and

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: they have started a qualifying business within the meaning of section 98.06 .

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: No more than five applicants are to be considered members of the start-up business class in respect of the same business.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: The Minister may enter into an agreement with an organization to provide for any matter related to the start-up business class, including

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the making of recommendations and the provision of advice to the Minister on the designation of an entity and on the revocation of those designations;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the establishment of criteria, standards of conduct and best practices for the making of commitments or the performance of other activities related to the start-up business class by an entity;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the making of recommendations and the provision of advice to the Minister on the operation of these Regulations with respect to the start-up business class;

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the establishment of peer review panels referred to in section 98.09 ; and

label: (e)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the submission of reports to the Minister on the activities of designated entities.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: In order to exercise the functions referred to in paragraphs (1)(a), (b), (d) and (e), the organization must have expertise in relation to the type of entity in question, namely,

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: business incubators;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: angel investor groups; or

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: venture capital funds.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: An organization may exercise the functions referred to in subsection (1) only when the following conditions apply:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the organization is in compliance with the agreement and the agreement remains in force;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: subject to subsections 98.12 (2) and 98.13 (4), the organization complies with requirements imposed under subsection 98.12 (1) and paragraphs 98.13 (2)(b), (c), and (f) and requests made under subsection 98.13 (3);

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the organization is in compliance with these Regulations; and

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the organization has expertise in relation to at least one of the entity types referred to in paragraphs (2)(a) to (c).

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: The Minister must designate the entities referred to in subsection 98.01 (2) according to the following categories:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: business incubators;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: angel investor groups; and

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: venture capital funds.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: The Minister may only designate an entity if

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: it is recognized for its expertise in assessing the potential for and assisting in the success of start-up business opportunities in Canada; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: it has the ability to assess the potential for and assist in the success of start-up business opportunities in Canada.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: A designated entity must respect the following conditions:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: it must continue to meet the requirements of subsection (2);

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: it must enter only into commitments that respect these Regulations;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: it must provide the Minister upon request with information on its activities related to the start-up business class, including information on foreign nationals with whom it has made commitments and the businesses referred to in those commitments;

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: it must, subject to subsections 98.12 (2) and 98.13 (4), comply with requirements imposed under subsection 98.12 (1) and paragraphs 98.13 (2)(b), (c) and (f) and requests made under subsection 98.13 (3);

label: (e)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: it must comply with the terms of its commitments and with these Regulations; and

label: (f)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: it must comply with any federal or provincial law or regulation relevant to the service it provides.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: If there is reason to suspect that an entity does not meet the conditions or has submitted false, misleading or inaccurate information to the Minister, the Minister may

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: suspend the entity’s ability to make commitments; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: refuse to consider applications associated with commitments made by that entity.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: An action taken under subsection (4) comes into force on the day on which the Minister issues a notice of the action to the entity and remains in effect until the earlier of the day on which the situation is resolved and the day that is nine months after the day on which the notice is issued.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: If there are reasonable grounds to believe that an entity does not meet the conditions set out in subsection (3) or has submitted false, misleading or inaccurate information to the Minister, the Minister may revoke the entity’s designation.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: The Minister must publish on the Department’s website a list of all entities that are designated and those that are suspended under subsection (4).

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: A commitment must be in a written or electronic form that is acceptable to the Minister and must be provided by a person who has the authority to bind the designated entity.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: A commitment does not respect these Regulations if the entity that made it charges a fee to review and assess the business proposal or to assess the business.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: If there is more than one applicant in respect of a commitment, the commitment must

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: include information on each applicant; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: identify those applicants that the entity making the commitment considers essential to the business.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: If there is more than one applicant in respect of a commitment, the commitment may be conditional on the issuance of a permanent resident visa to one or more of those applicants.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: The Minister must establish the minimum total amount that the designated entities involved in the commitment must invest by buying shares or other forms of equity in the applicant’s business.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: The Minister may establish different minimum investment amounts based on whether the commitment was made by a business incubator, an angel investor group or a venture capital fund and, for commitments involving more than one type of entity, may specify different minimum investment amounts for commitments involving different combinations of entity types.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: The Minister must establish the minimum investment amount on the basis of the following factors:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the number or projected number of start-up business class applicants and designated entities;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the proportion per year of start-up business class applications approved, withdrawn or refused, as well as the grounds for refusal;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the amount of investment received per year by start-up business class applicants from designated entities as part of a commitment;

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the number, type and industry sector of businesses started in Canada by approved start-up business class applicants per year and the average investment needs of start-up businesses of those types in those industry sectors;

label: (e)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the average amount of investment and number of investments made in start-up companies in Canada per year;

label: (f)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the level of investment usually required for a business started in Canada by a member of the start-up business class to be successful and for the member of the class to become economically established in Canada; and

label: (g)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: industry standards and best practices, as determined in consultation with organizations referred to in section 98.02 , designated entities or other relevant stakeholders.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: The Minister must publish the amounts established under subsection (1) on the Department’s website.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: For the purposes of paragraph 98.01 (2)(d), a qualifying business with respect to an applicant is one

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: in which the applicant provides active and ongoing management from within Canada;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: for which an essential part of its operations is conducted in Canada;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: that is incorporated in Canada; and

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: that has an ownership structure that complies with the percentages established under subsection (3).

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: A business that fails to meet one or more of the requirements of paragraphs (1)(a) to (c) is nevertheless a qualifying business if the applicant intends to have it meet those requirements after they have been issued a permanent resident visa.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: The Minister must establish

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the minimum percentage of voting rights that are attached to all the outstanding shares of the corporation that must be held by the applicant; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the maximum percentage of the total amount of the voting rights attached to all the outstanding shares of the corporation that may be held by persons or entities, other than qualified participants.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: For the purpose of paragraph (3)(b), a qualified participant is

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: an applicant in respect of the business;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: a foreign national who has been issued a permanent resident visa as a member of the start-up business class in respect of the business; or

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: a designated entity.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: The Minister must establish the percentages referred to in subsection (3) on the basis of the following factors:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the number or projected number of start-up business class applicants and designated entities;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the proportion per year of start-up business class applications approved, withdrawn or refused, as well as the grounds for refusal;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the average size of businesses for which commitments are made and the average percentage of voting rights held by applicants and designated entities;

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the average size of start-up companies in Canada and the average percentage of voting rights held by the founders of those companies and other investors in those companies;

label: (e)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the number, type and industry sector of businesses successfully started in Canada by approved start-up business class applicants per year and the most common ownership structures for businesses of those types in those industry sectors;

label: (f)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the ownership share usually required for a business started in Canada by a member of the start-up business class to be successful and for the member of the class to become economically established in Canada; and

label: (g)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: industry standards and best practices, as determined in consultation with organizations referred to in section 98.02 , designated entities or other relevant stakeholders.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: The Minister must publish the percentages established under subsection (3) on the Department’s website.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: An applicant must provide documentation to establish that they are a member of the start-up business class, including

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: written or electronic evidence, provided by an entity that was designated on the day on which the application is made, that indicates that the entity made a commitment with the applicant;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the results of a language proficiency evaluation referred to in paragraph 98.01 (2)(b); and

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: written or electronic evidence that they have the funds required under paragraph 98.01 (2)(c).

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: In evaluating an application in the start-up business class, an officer may, in addition to these documents, require the production of documents that are in the possession or control of the applicant or of the entity making the commitment and that relate to the applicant, the commitment or the business.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: If the officer is not satisfied that the entity assessed the applicant and the applicant’s business in a manner consistent with industry standards or is not satisfied that the terms of the commitment are consistent with industry standards, the officer may refuse to issue the permanent resident visa.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: If there is more than one applicant in respect of the same business and one of the applicants who was identified in the commitment as being essential to the business is refused a permanent resident visa for any reason or withdraws their application, the other applicants must be considered not to have met the requirements of subsection 98.01 (2) and their permanent resident visa must also be refused.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: An officer may request that a commitment, the applicants and designated entities party to the commitment and the qualifying business to which the commitment relates be independently assessed by a peer review panel established under an agreement referred to in section 98.02 by an organization that has expertise with respect to the type of entity making the commitment.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: The request may be made if the officer is of the opinion that an independent assessment would assist in the application process. The request may also be made on a random basis.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: The peer review panel’s assessment must be independent and take industry standards into account.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: An officer who requests an independent assessment is not bound by it.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: An officer may substitute their evaluation of the applicant’s ability to become economically established in Canada for the requirements set out in subsection 98.01 (2), if meeting or failing to meet those requirements is not a sufficient indicator of whether the applicant will become economically established in Canada.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: However, a substitute evaluation must not be conducted for an applicant who did not have a commitment from a designated entity on the day on which they made their application.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: A substitute evaluation made under subsection (1) requires the written concurrence of a second officer.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: An officer may inspect any organization that has entered into an agreement referred to in subsection 98.02 (1) in any of the following circumstances:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the officer has a reason to suspect that the organization is not complying or has not complied with any of the conditions set out in subsection 98.02 (3);

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the organization has not complied with those conditions in the past;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the organization is chosen as part of a random verification of compliance with those conditions; and

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: as part of routine monitoring activities, the organization is monitored to ensure that it respects those conditions.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: An officer may inspect an entity designated under subsection 98.03 (1) in any of the following circumstances:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the officer has a reason to suspect that the entity is not complying or has not complied with any of the conditions set out in subsection 98.03 (3);

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the entity has not complied with those conditions in the past;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: the entity is chosen as part of a random verification of compliance with those conditions; and

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: as part of routine monitoring activities, the entity is monitored to ensure that it respects those conditions.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: In addition, the powers set out in sections 98.12 and 98.13 may be exercised with respect to

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: a designated entity, if an officer is inspecting an organization in accordance with subsection (1) and an inspection of the designated entity is necessary to verify that the organization is in compliance with the conditions set out in subsection 98.02 (3); or

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: an organization that has entered into an agreement referred to in subsection 98.02 (1), if an officer is inspecting a designated entity in accordance with subsection (2) and an inspection of the organization is necessary to verify that the designated entity is in compliance with the conditions set out in subsection 98.03 (3).

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: The powers set out in sections 98.12 and 98.13 may be exercised with respect to a business that is the subject of a commitment by a designated entity with respect to the start-up business class if an officer is inspecting that designated entity in accordance with subsection (2) and an inspection of the business is necessary to verify that the designated entity is in compliance with the conditions set out in subsection 98.03 (3).

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: The powers set out in section 98.12 may be exercised with respect to a third party if an officer is inspecting an organization in accordance with subsection (1) or a designated entity in accordance with subsection (2) and an inspection of the third party is necessary to verify that that organization or that designated entity is in compliance with the conditions set out in subsection 98.02 (3) or 98.03 (3), as the case may be.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: When conducting an inspection in accordance with section 98.11 , an officer may, for the purpose of verifying that the organization or designated entity is in compliance with the relevant conditions,

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: require the organization, the designated entity, a business that is the subject of a commitment or a third party to provide the officer with any relevant document; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: require any employee or representative of the organization, designated entity, or a business that is the subject of a commitment or a third party to report at any specified time and place to answer questions and provide relevant documents.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: A failure to comply with an obligation under paragraph (1)(a) or (b) is justified if the person, organization, entity or business made all reasonable efforts to comply with the obligation or if the failure results from anything done or omitted to be done by them in good faith.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: Subject to subsection (7), when conducting an inspection in accordance with section 98.11 , an officer may, for the purpose of verifying that the organization or designated entity is in compliance with the relevant conditions, enter and inspect any premises or place in which business is conducted by the organization, the designated entity or a business that is the subject of a commitment.

marginal_note: Powers in place or on premises
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: When on the premises or in the place the officer may

label: (a)
marginal_note: Powers in place or on premises
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: ask any relevant questions of an employee or representative of the organization, designated entity or business that is the subject of a commitment;

label: (b)
marginal_note: Powers in place or on premises
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: require from the organization, the designated entity or the business that is the subject of a commitment any relevant documents found in the premises or the place for examination;

label: (c)
marginal_note: Powers in place or on premises
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: use copying equipment, or require that the organization, the designated entity or the business that is the subject of a commitment provide copies of those documents to be examined away from the premises or the place or, if it is not possible to make copies in the premises or the place, remove the relevant documents to make copies;

label: (d)
marginal_note: Powers in place or on premises
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: take photographs and make video or audio recordings;

label: (e)
marginal_note: Powers in place or on premises
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: examine anything in the premises or the place;

label: (f)
marginal_note: Powers in place or on premises
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: require the organization, the designated entity or the business that is the subject of a commitment to use any computer or other electronic device in the premises or the place to allow the officer to examine any relevant document contained in or available to it; and

label: (g)
marginal_note: Powers in place or on premises
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: be accompanied or assisted in the premises or the place by any person required by the officer.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: An organization, entity, or a business that is the subject of a commitment, must, on request, provide an employee or representative to attend any inspection referred to in subsection (1), to give all reasonable assistance to the officer conducting that inspection and to provide that officer with any document or information that the officer requires.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: A failure to comply with an obligation under paragraph (2)(b), (c) or (f) or subsection (3) is justified if the organization, entity, or a business that is the subject of a commitment made all reasonable efforts to comply with the obligation or if the failure results from anything done or omitted to be done by them in good faith.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: An officer and any person accompanying the officer may enter on and pass through private property, other than a dwelling-house, to gain entry to the premises or the place. For greater certainty, they are not liable for doing so.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: A person may, at an officer’s request, accompany the officer to assist them to access the premises or the place.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: In the case of a dwelling-house, an officer may enter it without the occupant’s consent only under the authority of a warrant issued under subsection (8).

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: On ex parte application, a justice of the peace may issue a warrant authorizing an officer who is named in it to enter a dwelling-house, subject to any conditions specified in the warrant, if the justice of the peace is satisfied by information on oath that

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: there are reasonable grounds to believe that the dwelling-house is a premises or place referred to in subsection (1);

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: entry into the dwelling-house is necessary to verify compliance with the conditions set out in subsection 98.02 (3) or 98.03 (3), as the case may be; and

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: entry was refused by the occupant or there are reasonable grounds to believe that entry will be refused or that consent to entry cannot be obtained from the occupant.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Start-up Business Class
own_text: [Repealed, SOR/2016-316, s. 6]

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Self-employed Persons > Self-employed Persons Class
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Self-employed Persons > Self-employed Persons Class
own_text: For the purposes of subsection 12(2) of the Act, the self-employed persons class is hereby prescribed as a class of persons who may become permanent residents on the basis of their ability to become economically established in Canada and who are self-employed persons within the meaning of subsection 88(1).

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Self-employed Persons > Self-employed Persons Class
own_text: If a foreign national who applies as a member of the self-employed persons class is not a self-employed person within the meaning of subsection 88(1), the application shall be refused and no further assessment is required.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Self-employed Persons > Quebec Self-employed Persons Class
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Self-employed Persons > Quebec Self-employed Persons Class
own_text: For the purposes of subsection 12(2) of the Act, the Quebec self-employed persons class is prescribed as a class of persons who may become permanent residents on the basis of their ability to become economically established in Canada.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Self-employed Persons > Quebec Self-employed Persons Class
own_text: A foreign national is a member of the Quebec self-employed persons class if they

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Self-employed Persons > Quebec Self-employed Persons Class
own_text: intend to reside in Quebec; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Self-employed Persons > Quebec Self-employed Persons Class
own_text: are named in a Certificat de sélection du Québec issued by Quebec.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: For the purpose of determining whether a foreign national, as a member of the self-employed persons class, and their family members will be able to become economically established in Canada, an officer shall assess the foreign national on the basis of the following factors:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: age, in accordance with section 102.1;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: education, in accordance with section 102.2;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: proficiency in the official languages of Canada, in accordance with section 102.3;

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: experience, in accordance with section 103; and

label: (e)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: adaptability, in accordance with section 105.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: A foreign national who is assessed on the basis of the factors set out in paragraphs (1)(a) to (e) shall be awarded the applicable number of assessment points for each factor set out in the provision referred to in each of those paragraphs, subject to the maximum number set out in that provision for that factor.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: Points shall be awarded, up to a maximum of 10, for a foreign national’s age on the date on which their application is made, as follows:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: 10 points for a foreign national 21 years of age or older but less than 50 years of age;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: 8 points for a foreign national 20 or 50 years of age;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: 6 points for a foreign national 19 or 51 years of age;

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: 4 points for a foreign national 18 or 52 years of age;

label: (e)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: 2 points for a foreign national 17 or 53 years of age; and

label: (f)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: 0 points, for a foreign national under 17 years of age or 54 years of age or older.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: The following definitions apply in this section. full-time means, in relation to a program of study leading to an educational credential, at least 15 hours of instruction per week during the academic year, including any period of training in the workplace that forms part of the course of instruction. ( temps plein ) full-time equivalent means, in respect of part-time or accelerated studies, the number of years that would have been required to complete the equivalent of those studies on a full-time basis. ( équivalent temps plein )

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: Points shall be awarded, to a maximum of 25, for a foreign national’s education as follows:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: 5 points for a secondary school educational credential;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: 12 points for a one-year post-secondary educational credential, other than a university educational credential, and a total of at least 12 years of completed full-time or full-time equivalent studies;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: 15 points for

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: a one-year post-secondary educational credential, other than a university educational credential, and a total of at least 13 years of completed full-time or full-time equivalent studies, or

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: a one-year university educational credential at the bachelor’s level and a total of at least 13 years of completed full-time or full-time equivalent studies;

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: 20 points for

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: a two-year post-secondary educational credential, other than a university educational credential, and a total of at least 14 years of completed full-time or full-time equivalent studies, or

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: a two-year university educational credential at the bachelor’s level and a total of at least 14 years of completed full-time or full-time equivalent studies;

label: (e)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: 22 points for

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: a three-year post-secondary educational credential, other than a university educational credential, and a total of at least 15 years of completed full-time or full-time equivalent studies, or

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: two or more university educational credentials at the bachelor’s level and a total of at least 15 years of completed full-time or full-time equivalent studies; and

label: (f)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: 25 points for a university educational credential at the master’s or doctoral level and a total of at least 17 years of completed full-time or full-time equivalent studies.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: For the purposes of subsection (2), points

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: shall not be awarded cumulatively on the basis of more than one educational credential; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: shall be awarded

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: for the purposes of paragraphs (2)(a) to (d), subparagraph (2)(e)(i) and paragraph (2)(f), on the basis of the educational credential that results in the highest number of points, and

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: for the purposes of subparagraph (2)(e)(ii), on the basis of the combined educational credentials referred to in that paragraph.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: For the purposes of subsection (2), if a foreign national has an educational credential referred to in any of paragraphs (2)(b) to (f), but not the total number of years of full-time or full-time equivalent studies required, the foreign national shall be awarded the same number of points as the number of years of completed full-time or full-time equivalent studies set out in the paragraph.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: A foreign national must specify in their application for a permanent resident visa which language — English or French — is to be considered their first official language in Canada. They must have their proficiency in that language evaluated by an organization or institution designated under subsection ( 4 ).

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: If the foreign national wishes to claim points for proficiency in their second official language they must, with the application for a permanent resident visa, submit the results of an evaluation — which must be less than two years old on the date on which their application is made — of their proficiency by an organization or institution designated under subsection (4).

marginal_note: Proficiency in English and French (24 points)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: Points for proficiency in the official languages of Canada shall be awarded up to a maximum of 24 points based on the benchmarks referred to in the Canadian Language Benchmarks and the Niveaux de compétence linguistique canadiens , as follows:

label: (a)
marginal_note: Proficiency in English and French (24 points)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: for high proficiency

label: (i)
marginal_note: Proficiency in English and French (24 points)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: in the first official language, 4 points for each language skill area if the foreign national’s proficiency corresponds to a benchmark of 8 or higher, and

label: (ii)
marginal_note: Proficiency in English and French (24 points)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: in the second official language, 2 points for each language skill area if the foreign national’s proficiency corresponds to a benchmark of 8 or higher;

label: (b)
marginal_note: Proficiency in English and French (24 points)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: for moderate proficiency

label: (i)
marginal_note: Proficiency in English and French (24 points)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: in the first official language, 2 points for each language skill area if the foreign national’s proficiency corresponds to a benchmark of 6 or 7, and

label: (ii)
marginal_note: Proficiency in English and French (24 points)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: in the second official language, 2 points for each language skill area if the foreign national’s proficiency corresponds to a benchmark of 6 or 7;

label: (c)
marginal_note: Proficiency in English and French (24 points)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: for basic proficiency in either official language, 1 point for each language skill area, up to a maximum of 2 points, if the foreign national’s proficiency corresponds to a benchmark of 4 or 5; and

label: (d)
marginal_note: Proficiency in English and French (24 points)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: for no proficiency in either official language, 0 points if the foreign national’s proficiency corresponds to a benchmark of 3 or lower.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: The Minister may designate, for any period he or she specifies, any organization or institution to be responsible for evaluating language proficiency and approve the language test to be used to evaluate that proficiency if the organization or institution

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: has expertise in evaluating language proficiency; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: has provided the Minister with an equivalency between its language test results and the benchmarks set out in the Canadian Language Benchmarks or the Niveaux de compétence linguistique canadiens , as the case may be.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: The Minister must make available to the public the names of the designated organizations or institutions and the approved language tests.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: For the purposes of subsection ( 7 ), service agreement means an agreement concluded between the Government of Canada and an organization or institution for the purpose of having the organization or institution supply the service of evaluating the language proficiency of foreign nationals.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: The Minister may revoke a designation of an organization or institution or the approval of a language test if

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: the organization or institution no longer meets the criteria set out in subsection (4);

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: the organization or institution submitted false, misleading or inaccurate information or has contravened any provision of a federal or provincial law or regulation that is relevant to the service provided by the organization or institution; or

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: either the Government of Canada or the organization or institution has terminated the service agreement.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > General
own_text: The results of an evaluation of language proficiency by a designated organization or institution using an approved language test are conclusive evidence of an applicant’s language proficiency for the purposes of subsection (1) and of paragraph 98.01 (2)(b).

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Experience
own_text: A member of the self-employed persons class shall be awarded assessment points up to a maximum of 35 points for relevant experience during the period beginning five years before the date of their application for a permanent resident visa and ending on the day a determination is made in respect of the application as follows:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Experience
own_text: 20 points for

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Experience
own_text: two one-year periods of experience described in clause (a)(i)(A) or (B) of the definition relevant experience in subsection 88(1) or a combination of two one-year periods of such experience,

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Experience
own_text: two one-year periods of experience described in clause (a)(ii)(A) or (B) of the definition relevant experience in subsection 88(1) or a combination of two one-year periods of such experience, or

label: (iii)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Experience
own_text: two one-year periods of experience described in subparagraph (a)(iii) of the definition relevant experience in subsection 88(1);

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Experience
own_text: 25 points for

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Experience
own_text: three one-year periods of experience described in clause (a)(i)(A) or (B) of the definition relevant experience in subsection 88(1) or any combination of three one-year periods of such experience,

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Experience
own_text: three one-year periods of experience described in clause (a)(ii)(A) or (B) of the definition relevant experience in subsection 88(1) or any combination of three one-year periods of such experience, or

label: (iii)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Experience
own_text: three one-year periods of experience described in subparagraph (a)(iii) of the definition relevant experience in subsection 88(1);

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Experience
own_text: 30 points for

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Experience
own_text: four one-year periods of experience described in clause (a)(i)(A) or (B) of the definition relevant experience in subsection 88(1) or any combination of four one-year periods of such experience,

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Experience
own_text: four one-year periods of experience described in clause (a)(ii)(A) or (B) of the definition relevant experience in subsection 88(1) or any combination of four one-year periods of such experience, or

label: (iii)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Experience
own_text: four one-year periods of experience described in subparagraph (a)(iii) of the definition relevant experience in subsection 88(1); and

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Experience
own_text: 35 points for

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Experience
own_text: five one-year periods of experience described in clause (a)(i)(A) or (B) of the definition relevant experience in subsection 88(1) or any combination of five one-year periods of such experience,

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Experience
own_text: five one-year periods of experience described in clause (a)(ii)(A) or (B) of the definition relevant experience in subsection 88(1) or any combination of five one-year periods of such experience, or

label: (iii)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Experience
own_text: five one-year periods of experience described in subparagraph (a)(iii) of the definition relevant experience in subsection 88(1).

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Adaptability
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Adaptability
own_text: A member of the self-employed persons class shall be awarded assessment points up to a maximum of 6 points for adaptability on the basis of any combination of the following elements:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Adaptability
own_text: for the educational credentials of the member’s accompanying spouse or common-law partner, 3, 4 or 5 points determined in accordance with subsection (2);

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Adaptability
own_text: for any previous period of study in Canada by the member or their spouse or common-law partner, 5 points;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Adaptability
own_text: for any previous period of work in Canada by the member or their spouse or common-law partner, 5 points; and

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Adaptability
own_text: for being related to, or for having an accompanying spouse or accompanying common-law partner who is related to, a person living in Canada who is described in subsection (5), 5 points.

marginal_note: Educational credentials of spouse or common-law partner
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Adaptability
own_text: For the purposes of paragraph (1)(a), an officer shall evaluate the educational credentials of the accompanying spouse or accompanying common-law partner of the member of the self-employed persons class as if the spouse or common-law partner were the member, and shall award points to the member as follows:

label: (a)
marginal_note: Educational credentials of spouse or common-law partner
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Adaptability
own_text: for a spouse or common-law partner who would be awarded 25 points, 5 points;

label: (b)
marginal_note: Educational credentials of spouse or common-law partner
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Adaptability
own_text: for a spouse or common-law partner who would be awarded 20 or 22 points, 4 points; and

label: (c)
marginal_note: Educational credentials of spouse or common-law partner
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Adaptability
own_text: for a spouse or common-law partner who would be awarded 12 or 15 points, 3 points.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Adaptability
own_text: For the purposes of paragraph (1)(b), a member of the self-employed persons class shall be awarded 5 points if the member or their accompanying spouse or accompanying common-law partner, on or after their 17th birthday, completed a program of full-time study of at least two years’ duration at a post-secondary institution in Canada under a study permit, whether or not they obtained an educational credential for completing that program.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Adaptability
own_text: For the purpose of paragraph (1)(c), a member of the self-employed persons class shall be awarded 5 points if the member or their accompanying spouse or accompanying common-law partner engaged in at least one year of full-time work in Canada under a work permit.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Adaptability
own_text: For the purposes of paragraph (1)(d), a member of the self-employed persons class shall be awarded 5 points if

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Adaptability
own_text: the member or their accompanying spouse or accompanying common-law partner is related by blood, marriage, common-law partnership or adoption to a person who is a Canadian citizen or permanent resident living in Canada and who is

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Adaptability
own_text: their father or mother,

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Adaptability
own_text: the father or mother of their father or mother,

label: (iii)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Adaptability
own_text: their child,

label: (iv)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Adaptability
own_text: a child of their child,

label: (v)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Adaptability
own_text: a child of their father or mother,

label: (vi)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Adaptability
own_text: a child of the father or mother of their father or mother, other than their father or mother, or

label: (vii)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Adaptability
own_text: a child of the child of their father or mother; or

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection Criteria > Adaptability
own_text: the member has a spouse or common-law partner who is not accompanying them and is a Canadian citizen or permanent resident living in Canada.

PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection
own_text: Subject to subsection (5), if a foreign national makes an application as a member of the Quebec investor class, the Quebec entrepreneur class, the start-up business class, the self-employed persons class or the Quebec self-employed persons class for a permanent resident visa, an officer may only issue the visa to the foreign national and their accompanying family members if they meet the requirements of subsection 70 (1) and, if applicable,

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection
own_text: in the case of a foreign national who has made an application under the self-employed persons class and their accompanying family members, who intend to reside in a place in Canada other than a province whose government has, under subsection 8(1) of the Act, entered into an agreement referred to in subsection 9(1) of the Act with the Minister under which the province has sole responsibility for selection, the foreign national is awarded the minimum number of points referred to in subsection (4); and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection
own_text: in the case of a foreign national and their accompanying family members, who intend to reside in a province whose government has, under subsection 8(1) of the Act, entered into an agreement referred to in subsection 9(1) of the Act with the Minister under which the province has sole responsibility for selection, the foreign national is named in a selection certificate issued by that province.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection
own_text: The Minister shall fix and make available to the public the minimum number of points required of a self-employed person, on the basis of

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection
own_text: the number of applications by members of the self-employed persons class currently being processed;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection
own_text: the number of self-employed persons projected to become permanent residents according to the report to Parliament referred to in section 94 of the Act; and

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection
own_text: the potential, taking into account economic and other relevant factors, for the establishment of self-employed persons in Canada.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection
own_text: A permanent resident visa shall not be issued to a foreign national as a member of the Quebec investor class, or to their accompanying family members, if the Minister is engaged in consultations with the province in respect of the interpretation or implementation of the agreement, referred to in subsection 9(1) of the Act and entered into under subsection 8(1) of the Act, between the province and the Minister in respect of the selection of investors and the consultations have not been successfully completed.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection
PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection
own_text: Whether or not a foreign national has been awarded the minimum number of required points referred to in subsection 108(1), an officer may substitute for the factors set out in subsection 102(1) their evaluation of the likelihood of the foreign national’s ability to become economically established in Canada if the number of points awarded is not a sufficient indicator of whether the foreign national may become economically established in Canada.

heading_path: PART 6 Economic Classes > DIVISION 2 Business Immigrants > Selection
own_text: An evaluation made under subsection (1) requires the concurrence of a second officer.
