heading_path: PART 7 Family Classes > DIVISION 3 Sponsors
own_text: If any of the following proceedings are brought against a sponsor or co-signer, the sponsorship application shall not be processed until there has been a final determination of the proceeding:

label: (a)
marginal_note: Suspension during proceedings against sponsor or co-signer
heading_path: PART 7 Family Classes > DIVISION 3 Sponsors
own_text: the revocation of citizenship under the Citizenship Act ;

label: (b)
marginal_note: Suspension during proceedings against sponsor or co-signer
heading_path: PART 7 Family Classes > DIVISION 3 Sponsors
own_text: a report prepared under subsection 44(1) of the Act; or

label: (c)
marginal_note: Suspension during proceedings against sponsor or co-signer
heading_path: PART 7 Family Classes > DIVISION 3 Sponsors
own_text: a charge alleging the commission of an offence under an Act of Parliament punishable by a maximum term of imprisonment of at least 10 years.

heading_path: PART 7 Family Classes > DIVISION 3 Sponsors
own_text: In respect of a proceeding to which subsection 63(4) of the Act applies, the sponsorship application shall not be processed until the later of

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 7 Family Classes > DIVISION 3 Sponsors
own_text: the period for making an appeal under that subsection has expired, and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 7 Family Classes > DIVISION 3 Sponsors
own_text: if an appeal is made, the final determination of the appeal.

heading_path: PART 7 Family Classes > DIVISION 3 Sponsors
own_text: If the sponsor resides in the Province of Quebec, the government of which has entered into an agreement referred to in paragraph 131(b),

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 7 Family Classes > DIVISION 3 Sponsors
own_text: the sponsor’s undertaking, given in accordance with section 131, is the undertaking required by An Act respecting immigration to Québec , R.S.Q., c.I-0.2, as amended from time to time;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 7 Family Classes > DIVISION 3 Sponsors
own_text: an officer shall approve the sponsorship application only if there is evidence that the competent authority of the Province has determined that the sponsor, on the day the undertaking was given as well as on the day a decision was made with respect to the application, was able to fulfil the undertaking; and

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 7 Family Classes > DIVISION 3 Sponsors
own_text: subsections 132(4) and (5) and paragraphs 133(1)(g) and (i) do not apply.

heading_path: PART 7 Family Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Collection and Disclosure of Information
PART 7 Family Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Collection and Disclosure of Information
own_text: The Minister may collect the social insurance numbers of a sponsor and a co-signer who have submitted an application to sponsor a person set out in clause 133(1)(j)(i)(B), in order to verify that they meet the requirements set out in clause 133(1)(j)(i)(B) and in paragraph 133(1)(k).

heading_path: PART 7 Family Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Collection and Disclosure of Information
own_text: The Minister may disclose the social insurance numbers of the sponsor and the co-signer to the Canada Revenue Agency for the purposes set out in subsection (1) if the Minister has entered into an arrangement with the Agency for the disclosure of that information.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Interpretation
own_text: The definitions in this section apply in this Division and in Division 2. group means (a) five or more Canadian citizens or permanent residents, each of whom is at least 18 years of age, who are acting together for the purpose of sponsoring a Convention refugee or a person in similar circumstances; or (b) one or more Canadian citizens or permanent residents, each of whom is at least 18 years of age, and a corporation or unincorporated organization or association referred to in subsection 13(2) of the Act, acting together for the purpose of sponsoring a Convention refugee or a person in similar circumstances. ( groupe ) referral organization means (a) the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees; or (b) any organization with which the Minister has entered into a memorandum of understanding under section 143. ( organisation de recommandation ) sponsor means (a) a group, a corporation or an unincorporated organization or association referred to in subsection 13(2) of the Act, or any combination of them, that is acting for the purpose of sponsoring a Convention refugee or a person in similar circumstances; or (b) for the purposes of section 158, a sponsor as defined in section 1 of the Québec Immigration Regulation , CQLR, c. I-0.2.1, r. 3, as amended from time to time. ( répondant ) undertaking means an undertaking in writing to the Minister to provide resettlement assistance, lodging and other basic necessities in Canada for a member of a class prescribed by this Division, the member’s accompanying family members and any of the member’s non-accompanying family members who meet the requirements of section 141, for the period determined in accordance with subsections 154(2) and (3). ( engagement ) urgent need of protection means, in respect of a member of the Convention refugee abroad or the country of asylum class, that their life, liberty or physical safety is under immediate threat and, if not protected, the person is likely to be (a) killed; (b) subjected to violence, torture, sexual assault or arbitrary imprisonment; or (c) returned to their country of nationality or of their former habitual residence. ( besoin urgent de protection ) vulnerable means, in respect of a Convention refugee or a person in similar circumstances, that the person has a greater need of protection than other applicants for protection abroad because of the person’s particular circumstances that give rise to a heightened risk to their physical safety. ( vulnérable )

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: A permanent resident visa shall be issued to a foreign national in need of refugee protection, and their accompanying family members, if following an examination it is established that

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: the foreign national is outside Canada;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: the foreign national has submitted an application for a permanent resident visa under this Division in accordance with paragraphs 10(1)(a) to (c) and (2)(c.1) to (d) and sections 140.1 to 140.3;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: the foreign national is seeking to come to Canada to establish permanent residence;

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: the foreign national is a person in respect of whom there is no reasonable prospect, within a reasonable period, of a durable solution in a country other than Canada, namely

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: voluntary repatriation or resettlement in their country of nationality or habitual residence, or

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: resettlement or an offer of resettlement in another country;

label: (e)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: the foreign national is a member of one of the classes prescribed by this Division;

label: (f)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: one of the following is the case, namely

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: the sponsor’s sponsorship application for the foreign national and their family members included in the application for protection has been approved under these Regulations,

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: in the case of a member of the Convention refugee abroad class, financial assistance in the form of funds from a governmental resettlement assistance program is available in Canada for the foreign national and their family members included in the application for protection, or

label: (iii)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: the foreign national has sufficient financial resources to provide for the lodging, care and maintenance, and for the resettlement in Canada, of themself and their family members included in the application for protection;

label: (g)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: if the foreign national intends to reside in a province other than the Province of Quebec, the foreign national and their family members included in the application for protection will be able to become successfully established in Canada, taking into account the following factors:

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: their resourcefulness and other similar qualities that assist in integration in a new society,

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: the presence of their relatives, including the relatives of a spouse or a common-law partner, or their sponsor in the expected community of resettlement,

label: (iii)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: their potential for employment in Canada, given their education, work experience and skills, and

label: (iv)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: their ability to learn to communicate in one of the official languages of Canada;

label: (h)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: if the foreign national intends to reside in the Province of Quebec, the competent authority of that Province is of the opinion that the foreign national and their family members included in the application for protection meet the selection criteria of the Province; and

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: subject to subsections (3) and (4), the foreign national and their family members included in the application for protection are not inadmissible.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: Paragraph (1)(g) does not apply to a foreign national, or their family members included in the application for protection, who has been determined by an officer to be vulnerable or in urgent need of protection.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: A foreign national who is a member of a class prescribed by this Division, and meets the applicable requirements of this Division, is exempted from the application of section 39 of the Act.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: A foreign national who is a member of a class prescribed by this Division, and meets the applicable requirements of this Division, is exempted from the application of paragraph 38(1)(c) of the Act.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: Family members of an applicant who is determined to be a member of a class under this Division are members of the applicant’s class.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: An application for a permanent resident visa submitted by a foreign national under this Division shall indicate that the foreign national is outside Canada and is making a claim for refugee protection and shall

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: contain the name, address and country of birth of the applicant and of all their accompanying family members;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: contain the name and country of birth of all the applicant’s non-accompanying family members; and

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: indicate whether the applicant or any of their accompanying or non-accompanying family members is the spouse, common-law partner or conjugal partner of another person.

marginal_note: Sponsorship of foreign national — requirement to attach applications
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General

marginal_note: Sponsorship of foreign national — requirement to attach applications
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: If the foreign national making an application for a permanent resident visa under this Division is being sponsored, the application for a permanent resident visa shall

label: (a)
marginal_note: Sponsorship of foreign national — requirement to attach applications
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: be accompanied by a sponsorship application referred to in paragraph 153(1)(b) by which the foreign national is being sponsored; or

label: (b)
marginal_note: Sponsorship of foreign national — requirement to attach applications
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: be attached to the sponsorship application sent by the sponsor in accordance with subsection 153(1.2).

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: The foreign national who has chosen to have their application for a permanent resident visa accompanied by the sponsorship application shall send the application for a permanent resident visa and the sponsorship application to the Department’s Case Processing Centre in Canada for processing those applications.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: If the foreign national making an application for a permanent resident visa under this Division is not being sponsored, a foreign national making an application for a permanent resident visa under this Division shall submit their application with one of the following referrals, if the referral has not yet been submitted to the immigration office by its issuer:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: a referral from a referral organization;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: a referral resulting from an arrangement between the Minister and the government of a foreign state or any institution of such a government relating to resettlement; or

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: a referral resulting from an agreement relating to resettlement entered into by the Government of Canada and an international organization or the government of a foreign state.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: A foreign national may submit the application without a referral if they reside in a geographic area as determined by the Minister in accordance with subsection (3).

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: The Minister may determine on the basis of the following factors that a geographic area is an area in which circumstances justify the submission of permanent resident visa applications without a referral:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: advice from referral organizations with which the Minister has entered into a memorandum of understanding under section 143 that they are unable to make the number of referrals specified in their memorandum of understanding for the area;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: the inability of referral organizations to refer persons in the area;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: the resettlement needs in the area, after consultation with referral organizations that have substantial knowledge of the area; and

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: the relative importance of resettlement needs in the area, within the context of resettlement needs globally.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: If the foreign national who is being referred under any of paragraphs (1)(a) to (c) or if the foreign national resides in a geographic area as determined by the Minister in accordance with subsection (3), the foreign national shall submit their application to the immigration office outside Canada that serves the foreign national’s place of residence.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: An application for a permanent resident visa made under this Division, its related sponsorship application made under Division 2 of this Part and all documents submitted in support of the applications, except the information referred to in subparagraphs 12.3(b)(i) and (ii), shall be returned to the person who sent the applications as a result of the choice made under subsection 140.2(1) if

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: in the case of an application for a permanent resident visa, the requirements set out in paragraph 139(1)(b) are not met; or

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: in the case of a sponsorship application, the requirements set out in paragraph 153(1)(b) and subsections 153(1.2) and (2) are not met.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: A permanent resident visa shall be issued to a family member who does not accompany the applicant if, following an examination, it is established that

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: the family member was included in the applicant’s permanent resident visa application at the time that application was made, or was added to that application before the applicant’s departure for Canada;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: the family member submits their application to an officer outside Canada within one year from the day on which refugee protection is conferred on the applicant;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: the family member is not inadmissible;

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: if the applicant is the subject of a sponsorship application referred to in paragraph 139(1)(f)(i), their sponsor has been notified of the family member’s application and an officer is satisfied that there are adequate financial arrangements for resettlement; and

label: (e)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: in the case of a family member who intends to reside in the Province of Quebec, the competent authority of that Province is of the opinion that the foreign national meets the selection criteria of the Province.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: For greater certainty, the requirements set out in paragraph 139(1)(b) do not apply to the application of a non-accompanying family member.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: Subject to subsections 25.1(1) and (6) to (8) and for the purposes of this Division, to be considered a family member of an applicant, a person must be a family member of the applicant

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: at the time the application referred to in paragraph 139(1)(b) is made; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: at the time of the determination of the application referred to in paragraph 141(1)(b).

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: The Minister may enter into a memorandum of understanding with an organization for the purpose of locating and identifying Convention refugees and persons in similar circumstances if the organization demonstrates

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: a working knowledge of the provisions of the Act relating to protection criteria; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: an ability abroad to locate and identify Convention refugees and persons in similar circumstances.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: The memorandum of understanding shall include provisions with respect to

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: the geographic area to be served by the organization;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: the number of referrals that may be made by the organization and the manner of referral;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: the training of members or employees of the organization; and

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > General
own_text: the grounds for suspending or cancelling the memorandum of understanding.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Convention Refugees Abroad
own_text: The Convention refugees abroad class is prescribed as a class of persons who may be issued a permanent resident visa on the basis of the requirements of this Division.

marginal_note: Member of Convention refugees abroad class
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Convention Refugees Abroad
own_text: A foreign national is a Convention refugee abroad and a member of the Convention refugees abroad class if the foreign national has been determined, outside Canada, by an officer to be a Convention refugee.

marginal_note: Person in similar circumstances to those of a Convention refugee
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad

marginal_note: Person in similar circumstances to those of a Convention refugee
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad
own_text: For the purposes of subsection 12(3) of the Act, a person in similar circumstances to those of a Convention refugee is a member of the country of asylum class.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad
own_text: The country of asylum class is prescribed as a humanitarian-protected persons abroad class of persons who may be issued permanent resident visas on the basis of the requirements of this Division.

marginal_note: Member of country of asylum class
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad
own_text: A foreign national is a member of the country of asylum class if they have been determined by an officer to be in need of resettlement because

label: (a)
marginal_note: Member of country of asylum class
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad
own_text: they are outside all of their countries of nationality and habitual residence; and

label: (b)
marginal_note: Member of country of asylum class
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad
own_text: they have been, and continue to be, seriously and personally affected by civil war, armed conflict or massive violation of human rights in each of those countries.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad
own_text: [Repealed, SOR/2011-222, s. 6]

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad
own_text: [Repealed, SOR/2011-222, s. 6]

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad
own_text: [Repealed, SOR/2012-225, s. 8]

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad
own_text: An officer shall issue a temporary travel document to a foreign national who has been determined to be a member of a class prescribed by this Division and who

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad
own_text: holds a permanent resident visa or a temporary resident permit;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad
own_text: does not hold a valid passport or travel document issued by their country of nationality or the country of their present or former habitual residence;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad
own_text: does not hold a valid travel document issued by the United Nations or the International Committee of the Red Cross and is unable to obtain such a document within a reasonable time; and

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad
own_text: would be unable to travel to Canada if the temporary travel document were not issued.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Protected Temporary Residents
PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Protected Temporary Residents
own_text: The protected temporary residents class is prescribed as a class of persons who may become permanent residents on the basis of the requirements of this section.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Protected Temporary Residents
own_text: A foreign national is a protected temporary resident and a member of the protected temporary residents class if the foreign national holds a temporary resident permit and

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Protected Temporary Residents
own_text: became a temporary resident under a temporary resident permit for protection reasons after making a claim for refugee protection outside Canada under section 99 of the Act; or

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Protected Temporary Residents
own_text: was issued a Minister’s permit under section 37 of the former Act after seeking admission to Canada under section 7 of the former Regulations or section 4 of the Humanitarian Designated Classes Regulations .

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Protected Temporary Residents
own_text: A foreign national destined for Quebec does not become a member of the protected temporary residents class described in paragraph (2)(a) if they have not received a selection certificate from the Province of Quebec.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 1 Convention Refugees Abroad, Humanitarian-protected Persons Abroad and Protected Temporary Residents > Protected Temporary Residents
own_text: In subsection (2), former Act has the same meaning as in section 187 of the Act and former Regulations and Humanitarian Designated Classes Regulations have the same meaning as in subsection 316(1) of these Regulations.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: The Minister may enter into a sponsorship agreement with a sponsor for the purpose of facilitating the processing of sponsorship applications.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: A sponsorship agreement shall include provisions relating to

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: settlement plans;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: financial requirements;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: assistance to be provided by the Department;

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: the standard of conduct expected of the sponsor;

label: (e)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: reporting requirements; and

label: (f)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: the grounds for suspending or cancelling the agreement.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: In order to sponsor a foreign national and their family members who are members of a class prescribed by Division 1, a sponsor

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: must reside or have representatives in the expected community of settlement;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: must make a sponsorship application that includes a settlement plan, an undertaking and, if the sponsor has not entered into a sponsorship agreement with the Minister, a document issued by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees or a foreign state certifying the status of the foreign national as a refugee under the rules applicable to the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees or the applicable laws of the foreign state, as the case may be; and

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: must not be — or include — an individual, a corporation or an unincorporated organization or association that was a party to a sponsorship in which they defaulted on an undertaking and remain in default.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: Paragraphs 13(1)(a) and (b) do not apply to the document referred to in paragraph (1)(b) issued by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees or a foreign state.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: If the foreign national has chosen to have their application for a permanent resident visa attached to the sponsorship application in accordance with paragraph 140.2(1)(b), the sponsor must send the sponsorship application and the application for a permanent resident visa to the Department’s Case Processing Centre in Canada for processing those applications.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: The undertaking referred to in paragraph (1)(b) shall be signed by each party to the sponsorship.

marginal_note: Joint and several or solidary liability
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: All parties to the undertaking are jointly and severally or solidarily liable.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: A party or a sponsor who defaults on an undertaking ceases to be in default

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: in the case of a sponsor who defaults on a financial obligation, when the sponsor has reimbursed the government concerned, in full or in accordance with an agreement with that government, for amounts paid by the government;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: in the case of a party, other than an organization or association, who defaults on a financial obligation, when the defaulting party has reimbursed any other party to the sponsorship, in full or in accordance with an agreement with that party, for amounts paid by that party;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: in the case of a sponsor who defaults on a non-financial obligation, when the sponsor satisfies an officer that they are in compliance with the obligation; and

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: in the case of an organization or association that was a party to a sponsorship and defaulted for any reason, when a period of five years has elapsed from the date of default.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: An officer shall approve an application referred to in paragraph 153(1)(b) if, on the basis of the documentation submitted with the application, the officer determines that

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: the sponsor has the financial resources to fulfil the settlement plan for the duration of the undertaking, unless subsection 157(1) applies; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: the sponsor has made adequate arrangements in anticipation of the arrival of the foreign national and their family members in the expected community of settlement.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: Subject to subsection (3), the duration of an undertaking is one year.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: An officer may, on the basis of the assessment made under paragraph 139(1)(g), require that the duration of the undertaking be more than one year but not more than three years.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: An officer shall revoke an approval given in respect of an application under section 154 if the officer determines that the sponsor no longer meets the requirements of paragraph 154(1)(a) or (b) or is ineligible under subsection 156(1).

marginal_note: Ineligibility to be a party to a sponsorship
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship

marginal_note: Ineligibility to be a party to a sponsorship
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: The following persons are ineligible to be a party to a sponsorship:

label: (a)
marginal_note: Ineligibility to be a party to a sponsorship
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: a person who has been convicted in Canada of the offence of murder or an offence set out in Schedule I or II to the Corrections and Conditional Release Act , regardless of whether it was prosecuted by indictment, if a period of five years has not elapsed since the completion of the person’s sentence;

label: (b)
marginal_note: Ineligibility to be a party to a sponsorship
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: a person who has been convicted of an offence outside Canada that, if committed in Canada, would constitute an offence referred to in paragraph (a), if a period of five years has not elapsed since the completion of the person’s sentence imposed under a foreign law;

label: (c)
marginal_note: Ineligibility to be a party to a sponsorship
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: a person who is in default of any support payment obligations ordered by a court;

label: (d)
marginal_note: Ineligibility to be a party to a sponsorship
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: a person who is subject to a removal order;

label: (e)
marginal_note: Ineligibility to be a party to a sponsorship
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: a person who is subject to a revocation proceeding under the Citizenship Act ; and

label: (f)
marginal_note: Ineligibility to be a party to a sponsorship
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: a person who is detained in any penitentiary, jail, reformatory or prison.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: For the purpose of paragraph (1)(a), a sponsorship application may not be refused on the basis of a conviction in respect of which a pardon has been granted and has not ceased to have effect or been revoked under the Criminal Records Act , or in respect of which there has been a final determination of an acquittal.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: If an officer determines that special needs exist in respect of a member of a class prescribed by Division 1, the Department shall endeavour to identify a sponsor in order to make the financial assistance of the Government of Canada available for the purpose of sponsorship. A sponsor identified by the Department is exempt from the financial requirements of paragraph 154(1)(a).

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: In this section, special needs means that a person has greater need of settlement assistance than other applicants for protection abroad owing to personal circumstances, including

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: a large number of family members;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: trauma resulting from violence or torture;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: medical disabilities; and

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: the effects of systemic discrimination.

marginal_note: Settlement in the Province of Quebec
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 2 Sponsorship
own_text: If the foreign national and their family members intend to reside in the province of Quebec, the sponsor must meet the requirements for sponsorship under the Québec Immigration Regulation , CQLR, c. heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3 Determination of Eligibility of Claim
own_text: For the purposes of paragraph 101(1)(c) of the Act, prior claim means a claim for refugee protection that was made under section 99 of the Act, other than a claim that was determined to be ineligible to be referred to the Refugee Protection Division under paragraph 101(1)(e) of the Act if the foreign national who made that claim is subsequently seeking to re-enter Canada in circumstances where they have been refused entry to the United States without having a refugee claim adjudicated there.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3 Determination of Eligibility of Claim
own_text: The following definitions apply in this section and sections 159.2 to 159.7. Agreement means the Agreement done at Washington, D.C. on December 5, 2002 between the Government of Canada and the Government of the United States of America for Cooperation in the Examination of Refugee Status Claims from Nationals of Third Countries, including any modifications or additions made in accordance with its terms. ( Accord ) claimant means a claimant referred to in paragraph 101(1)(e) of the Act. ( demandeur ) designated country means a country designated by section 159.3. ( pays désigné ) family member , in respect of a claimant, means their spouse or common-law partner, their legal guardian, and any of the following persons, namely, their child, father, mother, brother, sister, grandfather, grandmother, grandchild, uncle, aunt, nephew or niece. ( membre de la famille ) legal guardian , in respect of a claimant who has not attained the age of 18 years, means a person who has custody of the claimant or who is empowered to act on the claimant’s behalf by virtue of a court order or written agreement or by operation of law. ( tuteur légal ) stateless person means a person who is not considered a national by any state under the operation of its law. ( apatride ) United States means the United States of America, but does not include Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, Guam or any other United States of America possession or territory. ( États-Unis )

own_text: .Paragraph 101(1)(e) of the Act does not apply to a claimant who is a stateless person who comes directly or indirectly to Canada from a designated country that is their country of former habitual residence.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3 Determination of Eligibility of Claim
PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3 Determination of Eligibility of Claim
own_text: For the purposes of paragraph 101(1)(e) of the Act, the application of all or part of sections 159.1 to 159.6 and this section is discontinued, in accordance with subsections (2) to (6), if

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3 Determination of Eligibility of Claim
own_text: a notice of suspension of the Agreement setting out the period of suspension is publicized broadly in the various regions of Canada by the Minister via information media and on the website of the Department;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3 Determination of Eligibility of Claim
own_text: a notice of renewal of the suspension of the Agreement setting out the period of renewal of suspension is published in accordance with subsection (6);

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3 Determination of Eligibility of Claim
own_text: a notice of suspension of a part of the Agreement is issued by the Government of Canada and the Government of the United States; or

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3 Determination of Eligibility of Claim
own_text: a notice of termination of the Agreement is issued by the Government of Canada or the Government of the United States.

marginal_note: Paragraph (1)(a) — notice of suspension of Agreement
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3 Determination of Eligibility of Claim
own_text: Subject to subsection (3), if a notice of suspension of the Agreement is publicized under paragraph (1)(a), sections 159.2 to 159.6 are rendered inoperative for a period of up to three months that shall be set out in the notice, which period shall begin on the day after the day on which the notice is publicized.

marginal_note: Paragraph (1)(b) — notice of renewal of suspension of Agreement
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3 Determination of Eligibility of Claim
own_text: If a notice of renewal of the suspension of the Agreement is published under paragraph (1)(b), sections 159.2 to 159.6 are rendered inoperative for the further period of up to three months set out in the notice.

marginal_note: Paragraph (1)(c) — suspension of part of Agreement
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3 Determination of Eligibility of Claim
own_text: If a notice of suspension of part of the Agreement is issued under paragraph (1)(c), those provisions of these Regulations relating to the application of the Agreement that are referred to in the notice are rendered inoperative for a period that shall be set out in the notice. All other provisions of these Regulations continue to apply.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3 Determination of Eligibility of Claim
own_text: If a notice of termination of the Agreement is issued under paragraph (1)(d), sections 159.1 to 159.6 and this section cease to have effect on the day set out in the notice.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3 Determination of Eligibility of Claim
own_text: Any notice referred to in paragraph (1)(b), (c) or (d) shall be published in the Canada Gazette , Part I, not less than seven days before the day on which the renewal, suspension in part or termination provided for in the notice is effective.

marginal_note: Time limit — provision of documents and information to officer
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Claim for Refugee Protection — Time Limits > Documents and Information

marginal_note: Time limit — provision of documents and information to officer
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Claim for Refugee Protection — Time Limits > Documents and Information
own_text: For the purpose of subsection 99(3.1) of the Act, a person who makes a claim for refugee protection inside Canada other than at a port of entry must provide an officer with the documents and information referred to in that subsection not later than the day on which the officer determines the eligibility of their claim under subsection 100(1) of the Act.

marginal_note: Time limit — provision of documents and information to Refugee Protection Division
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Claim for Refugee Protection — Time Limits > Documents and Information
own_text: Subject to subsection (3), for the purpose of subsection 100(4) of the Act, a person who makes a claim for refugee protection inside Canada at a port of entry must provide the Refugee Protection Division with the documents and information referred to in subsection 100(4) not later than 15 days after the day on which the claim is referred to that Division.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Claim for Refugee Protection — Time Limits > Documents and Information
own_text: If the documents and information cannot be provided within the time limit set out in subsection (2), the Refugee Protection Division may, for reasons of fairness and natural justice, extend that time limit by the number of days that is necessary in the circumstances.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Claim for Refugee Protection — Time Limits > Hearing Before Refugee Protection Division
PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Claim for Refugee Protection — Time Limits > Hearing Before Refugee Protection Division
own_text: Subject to subsections (2) and (3), for the purpose of subsection 100(4.1) of the Act, the date fixed for the hearing before the Refugee Protection Division must be not later than

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Claim for Refugee Protection — Time Limits > Hearing Before Refugee Protection Division
own_text: in the case of a claimant referred to in subsection 111.1(2) of the Act,

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Claim for Refugee Protection — Time Limits > Hearing Before Refugee Protection Division
own_text: 30 days after the day on which the claim is referred to the Refugee Protection Division, if the claim is made inside Canada other than at a port of entry, and

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Claim for Refugee Protection — Time Limits > Hearing Before Refugee Protection Division
own_text: 45 days after the day on which the claim is referred to the Refugee Protection Division, if the claim is made inside Canada at a port of entry; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Claim for Refugee Protection — Time Limits > Hearing Before Refugee Protection Division
own_text: in the case of any other claimant, 60 days after the day on which the claim is referred to the Refugee Protection Division, whether the claim is made inside Canada at a port of entry or inside Canada other than at a port of entry.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Claim for Refugee Protection — Time Limits > Hearing Before Refugee Protection Division
own_text: If the time limit set out in subparagraph (1)(a)(i) or (ii) or paragraph (1)(b) ends on a Saturday, that time limit is extended to the next working day.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Claim for Refugee Protection — Time Limits > Hearing Before Refugee Protection Division
own_text: If the hearing cannot be held within the time limit set out in subparagraph (1)(a)(i) or (ii) or paragraph (1)(b) for any of the following reasons, the hearing must be held as soon as feasible after that time limit:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Claim for Refugee Protection — Time Limits > Hearing Before Refugee Protection Division
own_text: for reasons of fairness and natural justice;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Claim for Refugee Protection — Time Limits > Hearing Before Refugee Protection Division
own_text: because of a pending investigation or inquiry relating to any of sections 34 to 37 of the Act; or

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Claim for Refugee Protection — Time Limits > Hearing Before Refugee Protection Division
own_text: because of operational limitations of the Refugee Protection Division.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Claim for Refugee Protection — Time Limits > Appeal to Refugee Appeal Division
PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Claim for Refugee Protection — Time Limits > Appeal to Refugee Appeal Division
own_text: Subject to subsection (2), for the purpose of subsection 110(2.1) of the Act,

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Claim for Refugee Protection — Time Limits > Appeal to Refugee Appeal Division
own_text: the time limit for a person or the Minister to file an appeal to the Refugee Appeal Division against a decision of the Refugee Protection Division is 15 days after the day on which the person or the Minister receives written reasons for the decision; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Claim for Refugee Protection — Time Limits > Appeal to Refugee Appeal Division
own_text: the time limit for a person or the Minister to perfect such an appeal is 30 days after the day on which the person or the Minister receives written reasons for the decision.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Claim for Refugee Protection — Time Limits > Appeal to Refugee Appeal Division
own_text: If the appeal cannot be filed within the time limit set out in paragraph 1)(a) or perfected within the time limit set out in paragraph (1)(b), the Refugee Appeal Division may, for reasons of fairness and natural justice, extend each of those time limits by the number of days that is necessary in the circumstances.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Claim for Refugee Protection — Time Limits > Appeal to Refugee Appeal Division
PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Claim for Refugee Protection — Time Limits > Appeal to Refugee Appeal Division
own_text: Subject to subsection (2), for the purpose of subsection 110(3.1) of the Act, except when a hearing is held under subsection 110(6) of the Act, the time limit for the Refugee Appeal Division to make a decision on an appeal is 90 days after the day on which the appeal is perfected.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 3.1 Claim for Refugee Protection — Time Limits > Appeal to Refugee Appeal Division
own_text: If it is not possible for the Refugee Appeal Division to make a decision on an appeal within the time limit set out in subsection (1), the decision must be made as soon as feasible after that time limit.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: Subject to subsection (2) and for the purposes of subsection 112(1) of the Act, a person may apply for protection after they are given notification to that effect by the Department.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: A person described in section 165 or 166 may apply for protection in accordance with that section without being given notification to that effect by the Department.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: Notification shall be given

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: in the case of a person who is subject to a removal order that is in force, before removal from Canada; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: in the case of a person named in a certificate described in subsection 77(1) of the Act, when the summary of information and other evidence is filed under subsection 77(2) of the Act.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: Notification is given

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: when the person is given the application for protection form by hand; or

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: if the application for protection form is sent by mail, seven days after the day on which it was sent to the person at the last address provided by them to the Department.

marginal_note: Criterion — exemption from application of paragraphs 112(2)(b.1) or (c) of the Act
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: For the purposes of subsection 112(2.1) of the Act, the Minister must consider, when an exemption is made, any event having arisen in a country that could place all or some of its nationals or former habitual residents referred to in that subsection in a situation similar to those referred to in section 96 or 97 of the Act for which a person may be determined to be a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: Subject to section 166, a person applying for protection may make written submissions in support of their application and for that purpose may be assisted, at their own expense, by a barrister or solicitor or other counsel.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: A person who makes written submissions must identify the evidence presented that meets the requirements of paragraph 113(a) of the Act and indicate how that evidence relates to them.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: An application received within 15 days after notification was given under section 160 shall not be decided until at least 30 days after notification was given. The removal order is stayed under section 232 until the earliest of the events referred to in paragraphs 232(c) to (f) occurs.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: A person who has remained in Canada since being given notification under section 160 may make an application after a period of 15 days has elapsed from notification being given under that section, but the application does not result in a stay of the removal order. Written submissions, if any, must accompany the application.

marginal_note: Application that must be received within 15-day period — certificate
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: Despite section 163, an application by a person who is named in a certificate described in subsection 77(1) of the Act must be received within 15 days after notification was given under section 160. An application received within that period shall not be decided until at least 30 days after notification was given.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: A person whose application for protection was rejected and who has remained in Canada since being given notification under section 160 may make another application. Written submissions, if any, must accompany the application. For greater certainty, the application does not result in a stay of the removal order.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: An application for protection by a foreign national against whom a removal order is made at a port of entry as a result of a determination of inadmissibility on entry into Canada must, if the order is in force, be received as soon as the removal order is made. Written submissions, if any, must accompany the application. For greater certainty, the application does not result in a stay of the removal order.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: For the purpose of determining whether a hearing is required under paragraph 113(b) of the Act, the factors are the following:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: whether there is evidence that raises a serious issue of the applicant’s credibility and is related to the factors set out in sections 96 and 97 of the Act;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: whether the evidence is central to the decision with respect to the application for protection; and

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: whether the evidence, if accepted, would justify allowing the application for protection.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: A hearing is subject to the following provisions:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: notice shall be provided to the applicant of the time and place of the hearing and the issues of fact that will be raised at the hearing;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: the hearing is restricted to matters relating to the issues of fact stated in the notice, unless the officer conducting the hearing considers that other issues of fact have been raised by statements made by the applicant during the hearing;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: the applicant must respond to the questions posed by the officer and may be assisted for that purpose, at their own expense, by a barrister or solicitor or other counsel; and

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: any evidence of a person other than the applicant must be in writing and the officer may question the person for the purpose of verifying the evidence provided.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: An application for protection is declared abandoned

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: in the case of an applicant who fails to appear at a hearing, if the applicant is given notice of a subsequent hearing and fails to appear at that hearing; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: in the case of an applicant who voluntarily departs Canada, when the applicant’s removal order is enforced under section 240 or the applicant otherwise departs Canada.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: An application for protection may be withdrawn by the applicant at any time by notifying the Minister in writing. The application is declared to be withdrawn on receipt of the notice.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: An application for protection is rejected when a decision is made not to allow the application or when the application is declared withdrawn or abandoned.

marginal_note: Applicant described in s. 112(3) of the Act
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment

marginal_note: Applicant described in s. 112(3) of the Act
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: Before making a decision to allow or reject the application of an applicant described in subsection 112(3) of the Act, the Minister shall consider the assessments referred to in subsection (2) and any written response of the applicant to the assessments that is received within 15 days after the applicant is given the assessments.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: The following assessments shall be given to the applicant:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: a written assessment on the basis of the factors set out in section 97 of the Act; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: a written assessment on the basis of the factors set out in subparagraph 113(d)(i) or (ii) of the Act, as the case may be.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: Despite subsection (2), no assessments shall be given to an applicant who is named in a certificate until a judge under section 78 of the Act determines whether the certificate is reasonable.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: The assessments are given to an applicant when they are given by hand to the applicant or, if sent by mail, are deemed to be given to an applicant seven days after the day on which they are sent to the last address that the applicant provided to the Department.

marginal_note: Applicant not described in s. 97 of the Act
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: Despite subsections (1) to (3), if the Minister decides on the basis of the factors set out in section 97 of the Act that the applicant is not described in that section,

label: (a)
marginal_note: Applicant not described in s. 97 of the Act
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: no written assessment on the basis of the factors set out in subparagraph 113(d)(i) or (ii) of the Act need be made; and

label: (b)
marginal_note: Applicant not described in s. 97 of the Act
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: the application is rejected.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: A person in respect of whom a stay of a removal order, with respect to a country or place, is being re-examined under subsection 114(2) of the Act shall be given

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: a notice of re-examination;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: a written assessment on the basis of the factors set out in section 97 of the Act; and

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: a written assessment on the basis of the factors set out in subparagraph 113(d)(i) or (ii) of the Act, as the case may be.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: Before making a decision to cancel or maintain the stay of the removal order, the Minister shall consider the assessments and any written response of the person in respect of whom the stay is being re-examined that is received within 15 days after the assessments are given to that person.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: The assessments are given to an applicant when they are given by hand to the applicant or, if sent by mail, are deemed to be given to an applicant seven days after the day on which they are sent to the last address that the applicant provided to the Department.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4 Pre-Removal Risk Assessment
own_text: On request, an applicant shall be given a copy of the file notes that record the justification for the decision on their application for protection.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4.1 Designated Foreign National — Requirement to Report to an Officer
PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4.1 Designated Foreign National — Requirement to Report to an Officer
own_text: For the purposes of subsection 98.1(1) of the Act, a designated foreign national referred to in that subsection who has not become a permanent resident under subsection 21(2) of the Act must report to an officer as follows:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4.1 Designated Foreign National — Requirement to Report to an Officer
own_text: in person, not more than 30 days after refugee protection is conferred on the designated foreign national under paragraph 95(1)(b) or (c) of the Act; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4.1 Designated Foreign National — Requirement to Report to an Officer
own_text: once a year in each year after the day on which the foreign national first reports to an officer under paragraph (a), on a date fixed by the officer.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4.1 Designated Foreign National — Requirement to Report to an Officer
own_text: The designated foreign national must also report to an officer if requested to do so by the officer because the officer has reason to believe that any of the circumstances referred to in paragraphs 108(1)(a) to (e) of the Act may apply in respect of the designated foreign national.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4.1 Designated Foreign National — Requirement to Report to an Officer
own_text: In addition to meeting the requirements of subsections (1) and (2), the designated foreign national must report to an officer

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4.1 Designated Foreign National — Requirement to Report to an Officer
own_text: any change in

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4.1 Designated Foreign National — Requirement to Report to an Officer
own_text: their address, not more than 10 working days after the day on which the change occurs, and

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4.1 Designated Foreign National — Requirement to Report to an Officer
own_text: their employment status, not more than 20 working days after the day on which the change occurs;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4.1 Designated Foreign National — Requirement to Report to an Officer
own_text: any departure from Canada, not less than 10 working days before the day of their departure; and

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4.1 Designated Foreign National — Requirement to Report to an Officer
own_text: any return to Canada, not more than 10 working days after the day of their return.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 4.1 Designated Foreign National — Requirement to Report to an Officer
own_text: The reporting requirements in subsections (1) to (3) cease to apply to the designated foreign national on the day on which they become a permanent resident.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 5 Protected Persons — Permanent Residence
PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 5 Protected Persons — Permanent Residence
own_text: For the purposes of subsection 21(2) of the Act, an officer shall not be satisfied that an applicant meets the conditions of that subsection if the determination or decision is subject to judicial review or if the time limit for commencing judicial review has not elapsed.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 5 Protected Persons — Permanent Residence
own_text: [Repealed, SOR/2012-154, s. 8]

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 5 Protected Persons — Permanent Residence
own_text: For the purposes of subsection 21(2) of the Act, an applicant who makes an application to remain in Canada as a permanent resident — and the family members included in the application — who intend to reside in the Province of Quebec as permanent residents and who are not persons whom the Board has determined to be Convention refugees, may become permanent residents only if it is established that the competent authority of that Province is of the opinion that they meet the selection criteria of the Province.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 5 Protected Persons — Permanent Residence
PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 5 Protected Persons — Permanent Residence
own_text: An applicant may include in their application to remain in Canada as a permanent resident any of their family members.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 5 Protected Persons — Permanent Residence
own_text: A family member who is included in an application to remain in Canada as a permanent resident and who is outside Canada at the time the application is made shall be issued a permanent resident visa if

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 5 Protected Persons — Permanent Residence
own_text: the family member makes an application outside Canada to an officer within one year after the day on which the applicant becomes a permanent resident; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 5 Protected Persons — Permanent Residence
own_text: the family member is not inadmissible on the grounds referred to in subsection (3).

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 5 Protected Persons — Permanent Residence
own_text: A family member who is inadmissible on any of the grounds referred to in subsection 21(2) of the Act shall not be issued a permanent resident visa and shall not become a permanent resident.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 5 Protected Persons — Permanent Residence
own_text: For the purposes of subsection 21(2) of the Act, the following are prescribed as classes of persons who cannot become permanent residents:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 5 Protected Persons — Permanent Residence
own_text: the class of persons who have been the subject of a decision under section 108 or 109 or subsection 114(3) of the Act resulting in the rejection of a claim for refugee protection or nullification of the decision that led to conferral of refugee protection;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 5 Protected Persons — Permanent Residence
own_text: the class of persons who are permanent residents at the time of their application to remain in Canada as a permanent resident;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 5 Protected Persons — Permanent Residence
own_text: the class of persons who have been recognized by any country, other than Canada, as Convention refugees and who, if removed from Canada, would be allowed to return to that country;

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 5 Protected Persons — Permanent Residence
own_text: the class of nationals or citizens of a country, other than the country that the person left, or outside of which the person remains, by reason of fear of persecution; and

label: (e)
heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 5 Protected Persons — Permanent Residence
own_text: the class of persons who have permanently resided in a country, other than the country that the person left, or outside of which the person remains, by reason of fear of persecution, and who, if removed from Canada, would be allowed to return to that country.

heading_path: PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 5 Protected Persons — Permanent Residence
PART 8 Refugee Classes > DIVISION 5 Protected Persons — Permanent Residence
own_text: An applicant who does not hold a document described in any of paragraphs 50(1)(a) to (h) may submit with their application

label: (a)
